Declaring these six targets required six whole-worktree searches, and a census captures its entire output into a fact that ships in the snapshot. This repository's previous two snapshots hold whole file dumps on single JSON lines \u2014 tet29's longest is 57249 bytes, tet28's 34477 \u2014 so a search for a symbol this crate discusses re-captures those dumps. What such a search costs turns out to be a property of the instrument and the moment rather than of the symbol, in two separate ways. Scope: `render` matches 486 lines and 373271 bytes of this tree in the state the census was taken in, or 447 and 311672 with `.git/` and `target/` excluded as well; `NON_COVERAGE` 35 and 95637, `Findings` 23 and 57418, `check_file` 5 and 285, and the two symbols that do not exist yet nothing at all. Those numbers hold still because the trees they range over are frozen. Time: the same counts taken with this memo's own artifacts included do not hold still at all. `render` measured 529 lines and 1136689 bytes at one point in this memo's review and 550 and 1202134 later, with no source change in between \u2014 what grew was this memo's evidence log, now 59 records and 164392 bytes, and its snapshot, whose longest fact line is the 574898-byte capture of the `render` census itself. Grading a claim about census cost enlarges the thing the claim is about, which is the compounding thesis demonstrating itself. It is also the one part of this section no independent pass can confirm, along with the count of six searches: both range over this memo's own logs and snapshot, which a pass grading this memo must not open, so they are recorded here expecting to stay ungraded. What any pass can check, and what survives every way of scoping the count, is the ordering and its cause: censusing a symbol quoted at length in prior memos' captured snapshots costs orders of magnitude more than censusing one that appears only in source. `check_file` is this crate's own entry point, dispatched from both front ends, and returns 5 lines and 285 bytes \u2014 so what drives the cost is not whether the crate talks about a symbol but whether earlier memos captured text quoting it, and every memo added under `docs/design/` enlarges the next memo's census of anything those memos quote.",
263:   "text": "This memo was written against a single tree: commit b57bf8edb4c1eb59d8d86a8327179f43a9cb0829, \"design: anchor the residue at first proof, not at the last pass\", with no tracked source file differing from it. The reader who wants to re-take an observation should check that pin out first. Which tree each individual observation was actually taken against is not something this memo asserts \u2014 every observation carries its own working-tree marker, and `check` prints those states.",
353:   "text": "The disclosure goes in the whole-search record's label, and it costs nothing in schema. TET-28 already added exactly one record per `look --grep` whose job is to say where a search started rather than what it hit \u2014 a `Search` entry when the grep matched, a `NoMatch` entry when it did not, and never both. That record is the natural and the only correct home for a statement about what the search did not visit, because the exclusion is a property of the search and not of any file it found. Putting the text there buys two carriers already built: the memo's Facts table renders each extent entry's label and renders nothing else from it, so the exclusion set is on the page for a reader who has only the committed document; and the pin hashes the label, so two searches with different exclusion sets fingerprint differently even when the text they matched is identical. It should also be printed in what `look` returns, for the author reading it in the moment \u2014 but the printed string is the convenience and the label is the record, which is the opposite of the two shapes this project has already been burned by: a warning with no lifecycle, and a refusal trail missing the refusal that mattered.",
364:   "text": "The ticket's numbers are figures reported inside a memo, which makes them claims that were graded rather than measurements anyone here has made, so the effect was re-measured on this tree directly. A census of the symbol `NON_COVERAGE` over the tetel worktree returns 858,096 bytes from fifteen files. Fourteen of those files are tetel's own output \u2014 three rendered memos, three evidence ledgers, eight snapshot logs \u2014 and one, `src/report.rs`, is the source anybody grepping for that symbol wanted. With the three exclusions the same census returns 169 bytes from `src/report.rs` alone. Those are bytes grep handed back and bytes a fact would then store; what fraction of them reaches any given caller is a separate quantity, and a later section settles it, because the ticket's answer to it does not survive.",
386:   "text": "This design ran into its own subject before it could declare a single modification target, and the shape of that is worth stating rather than working around quietly. TET-28 requires a symbol an implementer is told to modify to be censused by a grep of the whole worktree. Every candidate symbol here was priced first: `look_grep` costs 709,469 bytes, `NON_COVERAGE` 858,096, `censuses` 691,562, `look_path` 688,776, `search_key` 633,291. The interesting number is not any one of them but the floor they share \u2014 roughly 0.63 MB is returned whichever symbol is asked for, because it is not about the symbol at all. Dropping snapshot directories and evidence ledgers alone removes between 95.9% and 99.9% of each. So the census requirement is today priced by tetel's own accumulated output rather than by the code being censused: two thirds of a megabyte comes back from grep, and is stored in the fact, per declared target.",
397:   "text": "Then the design paid the price once, deliberately, to declare `look_grep` \u2014 and the payment failed in a way that settles the ticket's sharpest question. The search ran and was recorded, but the harness returning results to the author refused to hand back 707,751 characters across 38 lines, and spilled them to a file. So this memo's author never read the output of their own census, while the fact minted anyway and the full 707,751 characters are shipping in the snapshot beside this document. The ticket asked any design to say which path it is changing, the return path or the retention path, and this is the answer from the inside: they are already separable, only the return path currently has a cap, that cap belongs to the harness rather than to tetel, and it fired. The census's own extent is the summary of the problem \u2014 ten files matched, eight of them tetel's own output, two of them the source anyone grepping for `look_grep` was looking for.",
507:   "text": "The ticket's sharpest question is whether the non-stationarity actually goes away, and the answer is no \u2014 it moves, and moving it is the point. Rendering a second memo into a scratch tree, touching no source, left the matched output of a search for the same symbol byte-identical while changing the exclusion list from one memo pattern to two. So the half the ticket complained about within a run is genuinely gone: an evidence ledger growing during grading cannot perturb a census any more, because the search never reaches it. But the exclusion set itself is a function of how many memos the tree holds, the design writes that set into the search record's label, and the label is inside the pin \u2014 so two censuses of one symbol against unchanged source will still pin differently either side of a render. That is not a leak that survived; it is the same fact about the world, moved out of the captured bytes where nobody could see it and into a sentence in the record where a reader comparing two pins is told immediately why they differ.",
518:   "text": "Nothing, and the answer has two halves, both of which can be shown rather than argued. The first is that the change cannot reach the check path at all: two exhaustive greps of the whole source tree find `Command::new` in only `observe.rs` \u2014 the grep inside `look_grep`, and `run_command`'s child \u2014 and `worldstate.rs`, where it runs git; and `observe::` in only `main.rs` and `mcp.rs`, which build a request and dispatch it, and `facts.rs`, where the single occurrence sits in a doc comment. Every other file in `src/` contains neither string, so nothing on the check or render path calls into the observe module or spawns a process. The second half is that there would be nothing to change even if it could: the `tetel fact` module states that extent, output and pin are set once at mint time and never appear in a revision event at all, so no code path exists that could rewrite them. The three committed memos keep the extents and pins they were minted with, whatever a `look` would do today.",
562:   "text": "This design was built against a pinned worktree, so every file range and command output cited below can be re-opened at that commit and read as this memo read it. One commit landed mid-run \u2014 the memo's own first rendering \u2014 and a few later observations were taken after it; it touched nothing under `src/` or `tests/`, so the source tree the memo reasons about is the same at both.",
617:   "text": "The ticket asks whether the fix for the pin defect is to digest the pin or to compare it separately. Neither, and the reason splits by which record wrote the pin. On the witnessed path \u2014 the only one the floor counts \u2014 a record's pin is a content fingerprint over an observation's labels, world markers and output, while a claim's pin where it exists is a git short hash lifted from prose; the crate's own fixture ledger is where the operand does exist, both its claims pinned `abc1234`. Those two can never be equal, so the comparison fires on every claim always where a claim pin exists, and on none of the memos this tool renders, where no claim carries one. On the ingested path it is worse rather than better: the pin is copied straight from caller-supplied input with no shape check, so a reporter could type `abc1234` and discharge the comparison by typing \u2014 the same defect the floor sidesteps by counting witnessed records only. Under either reading the comparison carries no information about whether a wording has been graded.",
621:     "clause": "the comparison fires on every claim always where a claim pin exists",
622:     "why": "The captured source says the record pin is carried for fidelity but is not used by check logic, so a pin comparison does not fire on claims with pins.",
627:     "rejected": "#[allow(dead_code)] // carried for fidelity; no check reasons over its value directly \u2014 see derived_kind\n    pub pin: Option<String>,"
639:   "text": "The channel itself is not what the ticket supposed. Asked to confirm that a claim's pin moves only when its citation list moves, the code says otherwise: nothing derives a claim's pin from the facts it cites. The pin is read out of the prose \u2014 a sentence of the form \"at pin `<hash>`\" sitting between the nearest heading and the ledger table \u2014 and the single value found there is stamped onto every claim in that table. That parser is for imported, hand-authored ledgers; it finds nothing in a memo this tool rendered, which is the first half of why rule 3 needed rebuilding.",
682:   "text": "Dropping the rule does not mean dropping the defect the ticket found. The divergence is real and it has a home: carry the predicate's world markers into `EvidenceRecord` \u2014 one field at read-back, in a type named on twenty-two lines across two modules \u2014 and let `check` report which tree each grading pass stood in beside the tree the memo's own facts were taken against. One branch must not be collapsed on the way: the ingested write path sets the marker list to empty unconditionally, with no input that could do otherwise, so an empty set means the tree is unknown and not that it differs. That is the same empty-as-value trap the visibility line has on its identity axis, and it wants the same treatment. Reported this way the observation is a fact a reader weighs, not a unit of work a pass completes by grading, which is exactly what the human-owed partition is for. It took this section three tries to reach a ground that survives, and the two it discarded were both claims of impossibility that this repository's own artifacts disprove.",
737:   "text": "Neither matcher covers both populations, but that is a fact about the two tried here and not an obstacle in the problem \u2014 a rule matching a hyphenated id while still finding the corpus's bare references is straightforward to write. What decides the question is yield, and the yield is not merely small but uncountable. One figure holds: no proposition in any rendered memo carries a bracketed citation-shaped id. Bare tokens naming a sibling id resist even being totalled. The count moves with tokenisation; it moves with reading, according to whether an endpoint of \"per C3-C5\" counts, whether a backticked `ungrounded: C99` counts, and whether \"tet28's C9\" is a sibling reference or a mention of another memo's claim; and it moves with ordinary editing, as this memo showed by rewording one of its own claims mid-run and dissolving a reference in passing. This design applied a standard to rule 3 \u2014 a rule that fires on nothing ever written here is not worth shipping \u2014 and it would be dishonest not to turn the same standard on a disjunct carrying a new reverse index, a traversal and borrowed machinery to schedule a set nobody can count twice the same way. The closure is deferred, and what it owes before it returns is a stated yield, not a better matcher.",
759:   "text": "One thing is worth recording about the machinery the closure would have needed, since it was built and then set aside. Check 5 already indexes the reverse citation graph and walks it breadth-first with a visited set seeded by the root, precisely so a citation cycling back terminates instead of looping, and that traversal transfers to a fixpoint over owed-ness cleanly \u2014 its two stated preconditions, that a self-citation is not a dependency and that ledger claims are excluded, both turn out not to bind at that destination. None of that is wrong. It simply has nowhere to land while the closure is deferred, which is why this memo carries no transplant.",
770:   "text": "The ticket suspects that N=2 and a rule to stop after the first round that provokes no revision may together prevent a design loop from terminating on its intended signal, since the first round cannot leave nothing owed. Within this design there is no conflict to have: the owed list is an input to a pass's schedule, no disjunct of the predicate reads it back, and nothing this feature writes records whether it was ever emptied. An owed list still non-empty when a run stops is therefore work declined, not an exit criterion unmet. Whether it also composes with the stopping rules a designer agent operates under is a question about that agent's own definition file, which lies outside this repository and cannot be checked from it \u2014 so this memo names it rather than answering it.",
814:   "text": "The blast radius of that extension is small, and the way this memo first got it wrong is worth keeping. By identifier, `grounding_provenance` is named in three files: its definition, field and zero-init in `checks.rs`, one call site in `lib.rs`, one printing loop in `report.rs`. From that this design concluded no test depends on its wording, which is false. Grep the strings the function emits rather than its name and two end-to-end test files appear, asserting on `SELF-GROUNDED` and on `cannot be determined from here`, one of them asserting the latter's absence. They are substring assertions and an appended count would probably survive them, but that is luck, not the census's doing. A census enumerates a symbol's occurrences and is silent about everything that depends on what the symbol produces \u2014 its own declared blind spot, and this memo walked into it.",
880:   "text": "Replaying the scheduling rule against that ledger is what shows the floor is load-bearing, but one figure has to be set aside first. That a floor of one retains none of the seven findings is true by construction: a discovery is a verdict no earlier workspace gave, so it cannot occur at the first workspace to read a wording, on this ledger or on any other. The measurement that means something is what happens above one. Seven substantive verdict changes occurred at all; five of them arrived from the second workspace, one from the third, one from the fourth; and capping distinct workspaces per wording costs 35, 51, 60 and 67 gradings at N of one to four, against 69 unbounded. So N=2 buys five of the seven for sixteen gradings, and every further step buys less for more. The floor is not a safeguard bolted onto a cost optimisation \u2014 it is the part of the rule that decides how much of what full re-grading was buying survives.",
913:   "text": "The ticket asks for four pieces to ship together, and it is worth being exact about the standing of each. One is measured: the replay's ordinal distribution and cost curve say what a floor of two buys and at what price. That is not the same as the figure the earlier draft of this memo led with \u2014 that a floor of one finds nothing \u2014 which follows from how a discovery is defined rather than from anything this ledger did. The closure and the visibility line are argued in this memo from what the code does, and nothing measures what their absence would cost. The fourth, pin-change detection, does not ship as a scheduling rule at all. Extending the measurement's standing to what is only argued would be the easiest way for this design to sound better than it is, so it does not.",
935:   "text": "That divergence is worth naming rather than smoothing over. On the correctness axis it is survivable for a reason specific to what an owed list is: the schedule settles nothing, no value of N marks a claim confirmed, and the full brief goes out unchanged whatever N is. On the discovery axis it is not benign, because the amount of grading scheduled is what decides how many findings a run would still reach. Two obligations follow. The floor in force must be printed by both renderers \u2014 cheap in text, not cheap in JSON, where the brief is a bare top-level array with nowhere for a document-level value to sit, so carrying it means wrapping the array in an object and breaking the contract the `--json` test asserts. This design takes that breakage deliberately rather than let the floor be invisible under one output mode. The second obligation is a stated default: both front ends reach the brief today with no floor argument at all, so a caller who supplies nothing must receive a defined value. That value is 2, chosen for the largest saving rather than because it is the only floor that saves \u2014 18 gradings of 69 against 9 at N=3, giving up two of the seven discoveries where N=3 gives up one. Whether that last one is worth nine gradings is a judgement the replay does not make, and a memo whose stakes answer it differently raises N. That is the whole reason the floor is a parameter.",
946:   "text": "The earlier drafts of this section stopped here and reported the question as undecided, on the grounds that a memo under active work has a reproducible marker while one whose repository had moved on never would again. The second half of that was simply wrong: a marker belongs to a commit, and a commit stays reachable. With the false half removed the question is decided rather than open, which is why this section now ends in a decision instead of a stopping rule.",
981:   "text": "One asymmetry the design cannot close, and should not hide. Every figure in the replay counts gradings not performed, and a grading is not performed only if some pass declines to perform it. Nothing here makes that happen. A brief emits an id, a proposition, an optional pin and a withheld scope per claim, with no instruction prose in either renderer, and the invariant that keeps every claim in the list is the same one this design refused to touch. The owed section is therefore an artifact a pass may act on, not a mechanism that reduces what it grades. The costs on the other side are unconditional, and the largest of them was missing from an earlier draft: `brief_file` today reads a memo and renders it, calling neither `evidence::load` nor `analyze_ledger` and touching neither the snapshot path nor the workspace identity, so giving it the owed list turns it into a second ledger-analysis driver \u2014 a change of kind, not a threaded parameter. Add the floor through two front ends, a shape change to the JSON brief, and the widenings in the check path. The saving is real only if passes use the list, and no claim here says they will, because nothing in this repository could check it.",
1040:   "text": "This memo designs one change with two halves. `look` decides for itself how much of an observation it returns to the author, and it says what it withheld in two places: in the observation's label, where a later reader of the memo finds it, and in the returned text itself, where the author finds it before writing anything about what they saw. The worktree everything below was read against is pinned: HEAD 81137aa683bdced9bf01a94d34c66b7f4a1758fd on branch tet30-prose-revised-since-proof, with every tracked path unmodified and unstaged and the only entries `git status` reports at all being the eleven untracked files this design itself wrote \u2014 the memo, its evidence sidecar and its snapshot directory. So a reader can re-run any of it against the same tracked bytes. Which of those states each individual fact was captured in is not asserted here: tetel records it with the fact and `check` reports it.",
1051:   "text": "`look_grep` already does the two jobs separately. It runs grep once, then builds `printed` \u2014 the string handed back to the author, which today is grep's stdout verbatim followed by a parenthesised exclusion note \u2014 and, independently, the pending entries: one `Search` record carrying the root, the pattern and a matched-file count, and one `GrepMatch` record per matched file carrying that file's matched lines. The two are derived from the same stdout but neither reads the other, and that separation is what the bound rests on: out of a bounded call, every entry's captured output, its key and its world-tree markers come back byte-identical to what they are today, so two observations of one root still overlap and a later reader still re-reads the same bytes. What does not stay identical is the extent, the pin and the fact that ships. `facts::mint` copies each entry's label straight into the extent and hashes label, world markers and output into the pin, and this design writes a shortfall segment into the label \u2014 so wherever the bound bites, all three differ from what they would otherwise have been. That is the point and not a cost. It is the same property the exclusion note was given when TET-46 chose to list the skipped memo paths rather than count them, so that two searches withholding different things could not fingerprint alike; a bounded search and a whole one should not fingerprint alike either. What makes f3 cheap, and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope, is narrower than \"nothing changes\": no new record, no second pass over the buffer, nothing read back out of the entries, no signature touched. One number is computed while `printed` is being assembled, and the label is built from that number. The direction matters to whoever implements this \u2014 bound first, label from the bound. An implementer who bounds `printed` and leaves the label alone has rebuilt the silent cut this memo exists to remove.",
1120:   "text": "The other `look` path turns out to have a different answer from the one its shape suggests. `look_path` computes `shown` and uses it twice, but not as one value in one place: `printed` is a string of its own that receives a *copy* of `shown` by borrow, and only afterwards is `shown` moved into the pending entry's `output`. Two independent strings exist between those two points, so a bound applied to `printed` there leaves the captured output, the label, the key, the extent, the pin and the snapshot byte-identical \u2014 the same separation `look_grep` has, in a function that reads at first glance as though it has none. There is therefore no code-shaped reason to leave the plain `look <path>` alone, and no other reason either: a whole-file read that overruns the caller's cap is the same silent cut this design exists to stop. So it is bounded too, on the same terms.",
1185:   "text": "Carrying that mechanism across brings its two preconditions with it. The donor states that a shortfall is not an error, and the same must hold here: hitting the bound returns a successful outcome with a bounded body, not a refusal. The code does not force that, and it is worth being exact about why, because the ordering invites the opposite reading: `printed` is assembled before any pending entry exists and the buffer is saved as the last act before the return, so an implementation that bounded while building `printed` could refuse there and discard nothing. What settles it is the crate's own rule about when to refuse. A refusal is for the case where nothing is left to tell and the remedy is singular \u2014 that is exactly how TET-28's census refusal justifies itself, against a check that stayed human-owed because only a person could tell context from conclusion \u2014 and every refusal in this crate's source is of that kind, a missing input or a forbidden flag combination, never a measurement of a result. A byte budget is not that: the number is a judgement, and an author who trips it has no act that re-runs the census smaller. Refusing would take the census away and name nothing to do instead. The donor also states that its key is the resolved path regardless of the range requested, which is what keeps two differently-sized reads of one file overlapping. That holds at the destination too: the `Search` entry is keyed by its root and each match entry by its file, both from paths alone, so a bounded search and an unbounded one of the same root overlap exactly as two unbounded ones would.",
1246:     "why": "The label includes the requested range even when b is no greater than the file length and no clamping occurs.",
1307:     "why": "For a range ending at line 20, the selected slice includes line 15 instead of stopping before it.",
1430:   "text": "All source observations below were taken against one worktree state: branch `tet30-prose-revised-since-proof` at commit `c821b94`, the commit that shipped TET-30's `prose-revised-since-proof` residue. The pin record at the head of this memo's evidence captured `git status` printing nothing at all. No tracked file was modified afterwards; nothing here was implemented. The tree has since gained exactly three paths, all of them this work's own output and all untracked: the memo, its snapshot, and its evidence ledger.",
1434:     "clause": "The pin record at the head of this memo's evidence captured `git status` printing nothing at all",
1478:   "text": "The sketch left the event's home open between `prose.jsonl` and a sibling log. The evidence closes it, and not on grounds of taste. `ProseEvent` is an internally-tagged enum over two variants, and the workspace's line reader turns any single unparseable line into an error over the entire log. A third variant is therefore not a compatible addition: I wrote a scratch workspace whose prose log held one ordinary `Create` followed by one `Ack`, and the build at this pin refused the whole file \u2014 including the `Create` it understood perfectly well. Every older build encountering such a snapshot would lose its ability to read prose at all, which is a far worse outcome than the residue line this design exists to clear. The field-level `#[serde(default)]` precedent already in both variants does not extend to a new variant.",
1489:   "text": "So the event lives in its own append-only log, `acks.jsonl`, and the snapshot manifest gains a tenth entry. Three properties, between them, make the failure direction one-way, and the third is the one I had to be shown twice. The manifest is the first: it is an explicit enumeration precisely so that shipping a new workspace file is a decision rather than an accident, so a build predating the entry never opens the file and prints exactly the listing TET-30 shipped. The second is that the ack log only grows, which holds cheaply here because the file does not exist yet: nothing in the tool today can remove or truncate a file it has never heard of, its only writer will be an appending verb, and no withdrawal verb ships. That was where an earlier draft of this section stopped, and stopping there was wrong. Monotonicity is a property of one workspace's log; the mechanism runs over a snapshot. Nothing binds a memo to the workspace that rendered it \u2014 the flag is free on every invocation \u2014 and the writer skips a file the current workspace lacks rather than removing it. So render a memo once from a workspace holding an acknowledgement, then again from a workspace that never held one \u2014 a rebuilt state directory, a second machine \u2014 and the old ack log survives beside the new prose and claims. That is a superset, not a prefix, and it suppresses a block the true state would list, silently. The third property closes it: the ack records the identity of the workspace that minted it, and suppression requires that identity to match the one the snapshot ships. A log from elsewhere is then void rather than honoured, and the failure returns to over-reporting.",
1511:   "text": "The brief called deletion and annotation both doctrine-compatible, and they are not equally good. Deletion loses a distinction the crate elsewhere insists on keeping: a report from which an acknowledged block has vanished cannot be told from a report on a memo where no post-proof revision ever happened, and this is a tool whose no-rows path exists precisely to say that two states which happen to both be quiet are not the same state. The cost of printing is also already paid \u2014 the entry format carries an author's own reason verbatim today, under `revised because:`, with the source comment insisting it is never paraphrased and calling it the most actionable line the entry has.",
1566:   "text": "Underneath those is the property that makes the rest cheap to reason about: the acknowledgement is a filter applied to the trigger's output, never an input to it. The set of blocks a reader is asked to act on can only shrink, so the design cannot invent a demand. A stale ack and an unmatched ack both simply fail to suppress, which is indistinguishable from no ack at all. A corrupt one is the case I first waved through and should not have. The line reader turns any bad line into an error over the entire log, and the one place this crate swallows that silently \u2014 the prose log at check time \u2014 defends the silence with a premise that does not transfer: that a corrupt prose log has already reddened provenance before the check gets there. Keeping acks out of `render` is precisely what makes that false for this file. So an unreadable acknowledgement log has to redden, joining the existing rule that drift and an unreadable snapshot are machine failures because both are objective contradictions decidable without a human. That is the single point where this design touches the machine partition, and it touches it for corruption of the record rather than for anything an acknowledgement means. It is also worth being clear what the digests do not buy: keying on them does not close TET-30's conceded blind spot for prose that ships alongside a claim revision. It only stops an acknowledgement outliving the state it attested to.",
1599:   "text": "Because the residue is computed against a snapshot and the snapshot is written by `render --out`, an ack minted after a render is invisible until the next one. That sequencing is not new and it is not this design's to fix: everything the check sees about a workspace it sees through the snapshot. What is this design's to decide is whether the acknowledgement changes the memo's bytes, and it must not \u2014 the determinism of `render` in the workspace alone is what makes a drift finding mean anything. Keeping acks out of the rendered output turns the extra render from an annoyance into a useful signal: it rewrites the snapshot in place and leaves the document byte-identical, so the discharge lands in version control as a change to the record with no change to the argument. That is a true description of what an acknowledgement is.",

896:    "prop": "\"Transcribed verbatim\" cannot be an honour-system field, and does not need to be: the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output. Both sides of that comparison are Strings the tool controls \u2014 a fact's output is produced only by look/run (file bytes read verbatim by look_path, grep match lines, a process's merged stream), no authoring surface lets anyone supply output by hand, and output is immutable after mint \u2014 so substring containment is a pure byte-level comparison with no normalisation step owned by the check. Typing is the selection mechanism, not the trust: the author types the premise, but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb. Two capture modes genuinely fight containment \u2014 grep-derived match outputs interleave \"lineno:\" prefixes between lines, and whole-search/no-match records carry empty output \u2014 so the design's guidance is that a donor fact is minted from `look` of the donor file; that is guidance about which observation to select from, not a new rule, since the relation is indifferent to which kind produced the bytes. 4744:    "prop": "Containment against a fact's whole output has one genuine unsoundness, and it is fixable by the same schema move TET-28 already made. Fact.output is built at mint by joining the buffer entries' non-empty outputs with \"\\n\", and the per-entry boundaries are not stored \u2014 so \"substring of fact.output\" can be satisfied by text straddling the seam between two observations: bytes that were never contiguous in anything the author actually saw, e.g. the tail of one file's capture concatenated with the head of another's. The fix is a serde-defaulted per-entry field on ExtentEntry recording the entry's output byte length, mirroring exactly how kind and pattern were added for TET-28: boundaries become reconstructible from lengths (skipping zero-length entries, matching the mint-time filter), the premise relation is then \"verbatim substring of a single observation's output\", and a donor fact minted before the field existed is ineligible with the same remedy TET-28 gives legacy facts \u2014 re-look and re-mint. Absent means not recorded, never guessed.",

6036:    "prop": "The refusals land on three surfaces, each the earliest that can decide its own question. (1) At the verb: quotation invariants \u2014 donor fact exists and is span-eligible, premise text is a verbatim substring of a single observation's output, destination is a live target, a discharge names an existing live claim. These are per-record and decidable at creation, exactly like target's census refusal. (2) At `render --out`: completeness \u2014 a live transplant with an undischarged premise (none cited, or its discharge claim withdrawn) refuses the write. This is deliberately later than the verb (the intermediate state is legal while authoring) and deliberately earlier than check (the ticket's placement): --out is the act that writes the reviewable artifact and its snapshot under the pinned policy that a rendered memo is never hand-edited, so a memo with a declared-but-unexamined premise should fail to come into existence rather than exist and fail; the remedy is singular \u2014 discharge the premise, or withdraw it or its transplant with --why. A preview render (no --out) still assembles, marking undischarged rows loudly, so mid-work visibility is preserved; this render/--out asymmetry is new, and it is the design's most debatable departure. (3) At check: re-verification of everything above against the shipped snapshot \u2014 both directions, since tampering can go either way (a transplant row the snapshot lacks; a snapshot premise whose text is not contained in its donor fact's output; a premise whose discharge claim is withdrawn or missing) \u2014 as a machine failure in the same partition as uncensused targets, with rows in a snapshotless document reported human-owed as unverifiable, the standing choice for snapshot-dependent findings. Containment is re-checked byte-for-byte from facts.jsonl, which already ships full outputs; check runs nothing and fetches nothing to do it.",

10619:    "prop": "There is no digest-shaped alternative in the sharp sense, and the reason is structural rather than an omission: `out_of_proof` can compare digests because a record carries a digest of the very text it graded, whereas nothing in the record shape names or digests a prose block \u2014 not `Subject`, not `Predicate`, not `RecordInput` \u2014 and the grounding brief deliberately hands a pass only id, proposition and pin. Giving a record a prose digest would require the grounding pass to read the prose it is supposed to grade blind. A weaker, genuinely clock-free alternative is constructible: have `render --out` append a publication record \u2014 per prose block its text digest, per claim its proposition digest and whether anything grades it \u2014 so the residue becomes an ordinal comparison between successive publications with no clock anywhere. It is rejected on resolution, not on cost. A publication log samples state only at the renders the author happens to perform, so a prose edit and the grading that preceded it inside one publication interval are indistinguishable, and the FORK-94 shape \u2014 grounding pass, then fix-round prose, then one render \u2014 falls entirely inside a single interval and would be missed. The timestamp comparison resolves exactly that ordering, which is why it is worth its stated bound.",
10651:        "text": "the grounding brief deliberately hands a pass only id, proposition and pin",
10707:        "note": "Second record for the brief clause: brief::build returns only id, proposition and pin per claim, so a pass is handed no prose at all."
10715:        "note": "BriefItem carries exactly id, proposition and pin, and the module doc says scope is withheld \"so an independent grounding pass can't see what the author declared the claim ranges over\" \u2014 the brief hands a pass only id, proposition and pin, so a prose digest would require the pass to read the prose it grades blind."
10719:        "note": "The structural half is exactly as stated and I confirmed it field by field: `Subject` carries only `name` (the claim id) and `digest` (sha256 of the claim proposition); `Predicate` carries verdict, pass, reported_kind, source, extent, world, note, pin, timestamp; `RecordInput` carries claim, pass, verdict, reported_kind, source, extent, note, pin. Nothing on any of the three names or digests a prose block, and `brief::build` hands a pass only `BriefItem { id, proposition, pin }`. What I could not establish is the rejection of the second alternative. That the publication-log design would miss the case rests on \"the FORK-94 shape \u2014 grounding pass, then fix-round prose, then one render\", which is an external trail this pass has no access to; and no publication-record mechanism exists in this tree to examine, so the resolution argument against it is reasoning rather than something source can settle. The claim's own hedge (\"this is not a claim that no third exists\") is honest and I am not disputing it."
10727:        "note": "BriefItem carries exactly id, proposition and pin, so \"the grounding brief deliberately hands a pass only id, proposition and pin\" is exact, and with F7 the sharp alternative's structural impossibility is established. The clause I cannot establish is \"Per the ticket's own account of the FORK-94 trail ... that is the shape the finding took\": the ticket is in a planning repository this pass must not open. The resolution argument against the publication-record alternative is reasoning about a mechanism that does not exist in this tree, so there is nothing here to read it against either \u2014 but it is stated as reasoning, not as an observation."

22437:        "note": "Every number reproduces on an independent re-run (35/51/60/67 gradings, 0/5/6/7 discoveries), but the one the design leans hardest on carries no information. A \"discovery\" is defined in this replay as a cross-workspace regrade giving a verdict no EARLIER workspace gave, so its ordinal is at least 2 for any ledger that could ever be replayed; the observed ordinals are [2,2,2,2,2,3,4]. Capping at one workspace per wording therefore retains zero discoveries by identity, on this ledger and on every other, including one where a floor would be worthless. So \"a rule with no confirmation floor would have retained none of the seven\" does not measure the floor's necessity \u2014 it restates the definition. Likewise N=4 retaining all seven is fixed by the maximum observed ordinal being 4. The empirical content of the replay is the ordinal distribution and the cost curve, and that content supports the weaker and still-useful proposition the memo could have made: five of the seven arrive at the second workspace, so N=2 buys 5/7 for 16 extra gradings. The sentence \"the floor is therefore what carries the discovery property\" is the one that spends the definitional figure as though it were an observation. Context worth stating: only 16 of the 35 pairs were ever graded by two or more distinct workspaces at all."
22445:        "note": "Every figure reproduces on an independent replay of tet30's ledger: 35 (claim, digest) pairs, 69 unbounded workspace-gradings, 7 discoveries at ordinals 5/1/1, the curve 35/51/60/67 at N=1..4, and N=2 buying five of the seven for sixteen gradings above the dirty-only floor. The final clause does not hold. \"Each further N buys less\" is false at the step this design's default turns on: N=2->N=3 costs 9 gradings for 1 discovery, N=3->N=4 costs 7 gradings for the last 1. The marginal price per discovery falls from nine to seven, so returns are not monotonically diminishing in cost, and the run also shows N=4 retaining all seven discoveries at 67 of the 69 gradings full re-grading performs \u2014 a cap at 4 forgoes nothing and saves two. The prose at memo line 11, \"every further step buys less for more\", carries the same error. This matters because that monotonicity is the stated reason for stopping low; the measured curve supports a floor over no floor, and supports 2 over 1, but does not support 2 over 3 or 4 by diminishing returns."

22670:    "prop": "The owed predicate as decided here: a claim is owed iff it is in `analyze_ledger`'s `ungrounded_claims`, or in its `out_of_proof`, or the pin stored on its records differs from the memo's currently stated pin, or fewer than N distinct non-author workspaces have a record whose `proposition_digest` equals the current proposition's, or `citation_ids_in` finds in its proposition text the id of a claim that is itself owed \u2014 the last computed to a fixpoint. Every disjunct is decidable from the memo, its evidence file and its snapshot, and each of the first four reuses a set the crate already computes.",
22690:        "text": "or the pin stored on its records differs from the memo's currently stated pin",
22718:        "note": "The third disjunct of the decided predicate is not well defined, on two counts, and the claim's closing sentence (\"each of the first four reuses a set the crate already computes\") does not hold for it. (a) \"The pin stored on its records\" is written as a single value; it is not. Replay of tet30's ledger: 125 records, 61 distinct pin values in that one file, and all 13 claims carry records with more than one distinct pin \u2014 C11 has 16, C10 and C12 have 8 each. The predicate does not say whether rule 3 fires when any, all, or the latest of a claim's record pins differs, and the three answers give different owed sets. (b) The comparison is between a per-fact `sha256:` content fingerprint (src/facts.rs 405-452) and a prose-parsed git token (src/ledger.rs 150-205), so no crate set is being reused here \u2014 unlike disjuncts 1, 2 and 4, this one is a new predicate over records, and it is the only disjunct with no existing computation behind it. Disjuncts 1, 2, 4 and 5 are unaffected by this record."
22722:        "note": "Four of the five disjuncts hold as stated and the closing summary is right for them. The third disjunct is not: \"the pin stored on its records\" is, on the witnessed path, `Some(fact.pin.clone())`, and a Fact's pin is `sha256:` + a hash over each extent entry's label, world_root, world_state and output (src/facts.rs:414-436) \u2014 never a VCS revision, whereas \"the memo's currently stated pin\" is a git hash parsed out of prose by `find_stated_pin` (the crate's own tests assert `abc1234` and `deadbee`). Compared directly, the two can never be equal, so this disjunct fires unconditionally on every witnessed-grounded claim rather than detecting a re-pin; the field that actually records the tree an observation was taken against is `world: Vec<worldstate::Marker>`, not `pin`. The final sentence is also over-broad on that disjunct: \"each of the first four reuses a set the crate already computes\" is true of rule 1 (`ungrounded_claims`), rule 2 (`out_of_proof`) and rule 4 (`by_others` inside `grounding_provenance`), but not of rule 3 \u2014 no check in the crate reads a record's pin at all (F5), so there is no computed set to reuse. \"Every disjunct is decidable from the memo, its evidence file and its snapshot\" is true as written (F7)."
22750:        "note": "The two checkable structural clauses hold in analyze_ledger: the first two disjuncts are its own `ungrounded` and `out_of_proof` outputs, and the digest-matched set the third needs (`fresh`) is a local that is never returned, so exposing it rather than recomputing is exactly what keeps one definition of \"graded on this wording\". The load-bearing sense of \"witnessed\" is confirmed at the record layer separately \u2014 `pass` is the workspace identity on the captured path and caller-typed free text on the ingested one. The four-disjunct predicate itself is the design's decision, not a fact of the tree; nothing I read contradicts it, and the pin rule's exclusion is independently supported by the marker replay."

23642:        "note": "True of the bound in isolation; false of the design, and the prose spends the unqualified form. `facts::mint` computes the pin as sha256 over, for every pending entry, `label` + `world_root` + `world_state` + `output` (facts.rs:417-435, its own comment: \"a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker\"), and copies `label` into the fact's extent (facts.rs:400-411). C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a \"showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)\" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes \u2014 the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests \"what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope\". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches \"would not pin identically\".\n\nThe second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries \"are built separately... neither reads the other\" \u2014 today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value (\"a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer\") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone \u2014 which is the design's own defect back again.\n\nWhat survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

The list already discriminates a withholding tetel chose (the tetel-output exclusion) from platform accidents that \"contemplate nothing tetel chose\" (grep skipping symlinked directories and binary files); a bound tetel applies to its own return is of the first kind. What the line states is a gap `check` genuinely cannot close: a fact's extent records the whole search, and nothing anywhere establishes that the author read all of it \u2014 `scope.rs` names that limit as permanently out of reach and does not claim otherwise.",
25575:        "text": "The list already discriminates a withholding tetel chose (the tetel-output exclusion) from platform accidents that \"contemplate nothing tetel chose\" (grep skipping symlinked directories and binary files)",
25623:        "note": "The claim's own generalising argument does not stop where the claim stops it, and the standing line it specifies will mislead by contrast.\n\nC15 argues correctly that a `NON_COVERAGE` line phrased about a search \"would leave every bounded path read with no standing statement anywhere in the list, which is the one surface this design nominates for the general case\", and concludes the line must say: \"what `look` returned to its author is bounded, and a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed while nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it.\"\n\nRun that argument one step further. `look` is not the only verb that writes an observation into the pending buffer and hands its author a return the caller then cuts. `run` does the same: `run_command` captures the child's merged stdout/stderr, pushes a `Proc` PendingEntry whose `output` is that capture, and returns it whole and unmeasured; both front ends hand it straight back with no size check \u2014 `print!(\"{}\", outcome.printed)` at src/main.rs:526 and `\"output\": outcome.printed` at src/mcp.rs:653-656 (F3). The `run` tool's own description at src/mcp.rs:649 documents the large case explicitly (\"a command whose output is enormous \u2026 puts that in a repository forever\"). So a `run` observation has precisely the defect this design exists to remove \u2014 the coupling between what was captured and what the author saw is broken by the caller, silently \u2014 and after f3 it is not merely unfixed but affirmatively contrasted against, because the new standing line names `look`.\n\nThe condition C15 does not state: its second half \u2014 \"a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed while nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it\" \u2014 is true of every fact in the ledger regardless of which verb captured it, but the line as specified scopes it to `look`. A reader of `check`'s standing non-coverage will reasonably infer the caveat does not apply to `run`-captured facts, which is exactly backwards: those are the ones with no bound, no shortfall segment and no trace at all.\n\nNot a demand that f3 bound `run` \u2014 that is a scoping decision the design may keep. What is owed is either a line whose general half is not verb-scoped, or a stated reason why `run` is excluded from a statement the design itself calls the general case."

Reading it as naming the second half (\"a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed, and nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it\") requires stretching \"insincere examination\" from not-examined to not-shown, and scope.rs does not spell that out. 25777:        "note": "The claim's own generalising argument does not stop where the claim stops it, and the standing line it specifies will mislead by contrast.\n\nC15 argues correctly that a `NON_COVERAGE` line phrased about a search \"would leave every bounded path read with no standing statement anywhere in the list, which is the one surface this design nominates for the general case\", and concludes the line must say: \"what `look` returned to its author is bounded, and a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed while nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it.\"\n\nRun that argument one step further. `look` is not the only verb that writes an observation into the pending buffer and hands its author a return the caller then cuts. `run` does the same: `run_command` captures the child's merged stdout/stderr, pushes a `Proc` PendingEntry whose `output` is that capture, and returns it whole and unmeasured; both front ends hand it straight back with no size check \u2014 `print!(\"{}\", outcome.printed)` at src/main.rs:526 and `\"output\": outcome.printed` at src/mcp.rs:653-656 (F3). The `run` tool's own description at src/mcp.rs:649 documents the large case explicitly (\"a command whose output is enormous \u2026 puts that in a repository forever\"). So a `run` observation has precisely the defect this design exists to remove \u2014 the coupling between what was captured and what the author saw is broken by the caller, silently \u2014 and after f3 it is not merely unfixed but affirmatively contrasted against, because the new standing line names `look`.\n\nThe condition C15 does not state: its second half \u2014 \"a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed while nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it\" \u2014 is true of every fact in the ledger regardless of which verb captured it, but the line as specified scopes it to `look`. A reader of `check`'s standing non-coverage will reasonably infer the caveat does not apply to `run`-captured facts, which is exactly backwards: those are the ones with no bound, no shortfall segment and no trace at all.\n\nNot a demand that f3 bound `run` \u2014 that is a scoping decision the design may keep. What is owed is either a line whose general half is not verb-scoped, or a stated reason why `run` is excluded from a statement the design itself calls the general case."

Reconciling over that constant leaves a tenth file a newer build wrote entirely unvisited by an older build's render, so the snapshot means \"the workspace at last render, for the files the rendering build's manifest names, plus whatever any other build left behind\" \u2014 which is the equality the claim says the fix establishes, and it is not established for the file this design adds. Reconciling over the snapshot directory instead does establish it, at the price of an older build deleting snapshot content it does not understand \u2014 a cost this memo never weighs, and a direct tension with `SNAPSHOT_FILES`' stated purpose that shipping or withholding a file be a deliberate per-build decision. Note the same residual hazard is what C14 cites to kill the withdrawal verb, so the two claims are consistent only under the manifest reading \u2014 under which this sentence's stated purpose is not achieved."

So a second workspace's render does leave a first workspace's acks.jsonl in place beside the second's prose/claims, while identity.json is overwritten \u2014 which is exactly the asymmetry the third (identity-equality) property closes."

The rule is only consulted for a block the trigger already listed, and listing means the current pair's first-appearance timestamp already exceeds the anchor; an ack recording that same current pair is appended to an append-only log by the same authoring workspace, after that pair exists, and stamped by the same `workspace::now_unix()` that stamped the prose event. So unless the authoring machine's clock runs backwards between the two appends, the ack's timestamp exceeds the block timestamp which already exceeds the anchor, and the clause is satisfied in every case it is evaluated. "Transcribed verbatim" cannot be an honour-system field, and does not need to be: the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output. Both sides of that comparison are Strings the tool controls — a fact's output is produced only by look/run (file bytes read verbatim by look_path, grep match lines, a process's merged stream), no authoring surface lets anyone supply output by hand, and output is immutable after mint — so substring containment is a pure byte-level comparison with no normalisation step owned by the check. Typing is the selection mechanism, not the trust: the author types the premise, but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb. This is exactly the README's Direction item for supporting-span selection ("refused unless it is a verbatim substring of a cited fact — the author cannot type an extent, and here could not invent support, only select it"), and TET-29 is the first place it becomes load-bearing rather than roadmap.

A "## Transplants" section renders beside the modification-target section: per live transplant, the donor fact id with its extent labels (labels, never absolute keys — the committed-document rule), the destination target id and symbol, and one entry per live premise carrying the selected text verbatim in a fenced block with the discharging claim id beside it; withdrawn transplants and premises are dropped, and once any claim exists the section renders even when empty ("none declared"), because the hole is the finding — the same visibility answer to under-declaration the target section shipped. Fenced blocks rather than table cells because a premise legitimately spans lines and markdown table cells cannot carry multi-line verbatim text without escaping, which would violate byte-fidelity.

The sharp one \u2014 a record carrying a digest of the prose it vouches for, the exact analogue of `out_of_proof` \u2014 cannot be built, for a structural reason rather than an oversight. `out_of_proof` compares digests because a record carries a digest of the very text it graded. No record names or digests a prose block anywhere in its shape, and the brief a pass receives is id, proposition and pin. Putting a prose digest into a record would mean the grounding pass reading the prose it exists to grade blind, which trades the independence the whole loop is built on for a residue line. The weaker one is genuinely constructible and was worked through rather than waved away: `render --out` could append a publication record \u2014 each prose block's text digest, each claim's proposition digest and whether anything grades it \u2014 and the residue would then be an ordinal comparison between successive publications with no clock in it at all. It is rejected on resolution, and the reason is structural too. A log that samples only when the author renders cannot order two events that fall inside one interval, and a grading followed by a prose edit followed by a single render is one interval. On the ticket's own account, that is the shape the finding took. The clock-free formulation would have been silent on it. That is the trade, stated plainly: the timestamp comparison buys the one ordering an interval-sampled log cannot, and pays for it with a bound it prints.",

/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_classify_v1.json:273:   "text": "The disclosure goes in the whole-search record's label, and it costs nothing in schema. TET-28 already added exactly one record per `look --grep` whose job is to say where a search started rather than what it hit \u2014 a `Search` entry when the grep matched, a `NoMatch` entry when it did not, and never both. That record is the natural and the only correct home for a statement about what the search did not visit, because the exclusion is a property of the search and not of any file it found. Putting the text there buys two carriers already built: the memo's Facts table renders each extent entry's label and renders nothing else from it, so the exclusion set is on the page for a reader who has only the committed document; and the pin hashes the label, so two searches with different exclusion sets fingerprint differently even when the text they matched is identical. It should also be printed in what `look` returns, for the author reading it in the moment \u2014 but the printed string is the convenience and the label is the record, which is the opposite of the two shapes this project has already been burned by: a warning with no lifecycle, and a refusal trail missing the refusal that mattered.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_classify_v1.json:450:   "text": "The ticket's sharpest question is whether the non-stationarity actually goes away, and the answer is no \u2014 it moves, and moving it is the point. Rendering a second memo into a scratch tree, touching no source, left the matched output of a search for the same symbol byte-identical while changing the exclusion list from one memo pattern to two. So the half the ticket complained about within a run is genuinely gone: an evidence ledger growing during grading cannot perturb a census any more, because the search never reaches it. But the exclusion set itself is a function of how many memos the tree holds, the design writes that set into the search record's label, and the label is inside the pin \u2014 so two censuses of one symbol against unchanged source will still pin differently either side of a render. That is not a leak that survived; it is the same fact about the world, moved out of the captured bytes where nobody could see it and into a sentence in the record where a reader comparing two pins is told immediately why they differ.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_classify_v1.json:462:   "text": "Nothing, and the answer has two halves, both of which can be shown rather than argued. The first is that the change cannot reach the check path at all: two exhaustive greps of the whole source tree find `Command::new` in only `observe.rs` \u2014 the grep inside `look_grep`, and `run_command`'s child \u2014 and `worldstate.rs`, where it runs git; and `observe::` in only `main.rs` and `mcp.rs`, which build a request and dispatch it, and `facts.rs`, where the single occurrence sits in a doc comment. Every other file in `src/` contains neither string, so nothing on the check or render path calls into the observe module or spawns a process. The second half is that there would be nothing to change even if it could: the `tetel fact` module states that extent, output and pin are set once at mint time and never appear in a revision event at all, so no code path exists that could rewrite them. The three committed memos keep the extents and pins they were minted with, whatever a `look` would do today.",

On the witnessed path \u2014 the only one the floor counts \u2014 a record's pin is a content fingerprint over an observation's labels, world markers and output, while a claim's pin where it exists is a git short hash lifted from prose; the crate's own fixture ledger is where the operand does exist, both its claims pinned `abc1234`. Those two can never be equal, so the comparison fires on every claim always where a claim pin exists, and on none of the memos this tool renders, where no claim carries one. On the ingested path it is worse rather than better: the pin is copied straight from caller-supplied input with no shape check, so a reporter could type `abc1234` and discharge the comparison by typing \u2014 the same defect the floor sidesteps by counting witnessed records only. /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_classify_v1.json:881:   "text": "The ticket asks for four pieces to ship together, and it is worth being exact about the standing of each. /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_classify_v1.json:954:   "text": "One asymmetry the design cannot close, and should not hide. Every figure in the replay counts gradings not performed, and a grading is not performed only if some pass declines to perform it. Nothing here makes that happen. A brief emits an id, a proposition, an optional pin and a withheld scope per claim, with no instruction prose in either renderer, and the invariant that keeps every claim in the list is the same one this design refused to touch. The owed section is therefore an artifact a pass may act on, not a mechanism that reduces what it grades. The costs on the other side are unconditional, and the largest of them was missing from an earlier draft: `brief_file` today reads a memo and renders it, calling neither `evidence::load` nor `analyze_ledger` and touching neither the snapshot path nor the workspace identity, so giving it the owed list turns it into a second ledger-analysis driver \u2014 a change of kind, not a threaded parameter. Add the floor through two front ends, a shape change to the JSON brief, and the widenings in the check path. The saving is real only if passes use the list, and no claim here says they will, because nothing in this repository could check it.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_classify_v1.json:1002:   "text": "`look_grep` already does the two jobs separately. It runs grep once, then builds `printed` \u2014 the string handed back to the author, which today is grep's stdout verbatim followed by a parenthesised exclusion note \u2014 and, independently, the pending entries: one `Search` record carrying the root, the pattern and a matched-file count, and one `GrepMatch` record per matched file carrying that file's matched lines. The two are derived from the same stdout but neither reads the other, and that separation is what the bound rests on: out of a bounded call, every entry's captured output, its key and its world-tree markers come back byte-identical to what they are today, so two observations of one root still overlap and a later reader still re-reads the same bytes. What does not stay identical is the extent, the pin and the fact that ships. `facts::mint` copies each entry's label straight into the extent and hashes label, world markers and output into the pin, and this design writes a shortfall segment into the label \u2014 so wherever the bound bites, all three differ from what they would otherwise have been. That is the point and not a cost. It is the same property the exclusion note was given when TET-46 chose to list the skipped memo paths rather than count them, so that two searches withholding different things could not fingerprint alike; a bounded search and a whole one should not fingerprint alike either. What makes f3 cheap, and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope, is narrower than \"nothing changes\": no new record, no second pass over the buffer, nothing read back out of the entries, no signature touched. One number is computed while `printed` is being assembled, and the label is built from that number. The direction matters to whoever implements this \u2014 bound first, label from the bound. An implementer who bounds `printed` and leaves the label alone has rebuilt the silent cut this memo exists to remove.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_classify_v1.json:1083:   "text": "The other `look` path turns out to have a different answer from the one its shape suggests. `look_path` computes `shown` and uses it twice, but not as one value in one place: `printed` is a string of its own that receives a *copy* of `shown` by borrow, and only afterwards is `shown` moved into the pending entry's `output`. Two independent strings exist between those two points, so a bound applied to `printed` there leaves the captured output, the label, the key, the extent, the pin and the snapshot byte-identical \u2014 the same separation `look_grep` has, in a function that reads at first glance as though it has none. There is therefore no code-shaped reason to leave the plain `look <path>` alone, and no other reason either: a whole-file read that overruns the caller's cap is the same silent cut this design exists to stop. So it is bounded too, on the same terms.",

The sharp one \u2014 a record carrying a digest of the prose it vouches for, the exact analogue of `out_of_proof` \u2014 cannot be built, for a structural reason rather than an oversight. `out_of_proof` compares digests because a record carries a digest of the very text it graded. No record names or digests a prose block anywhere in its shape, and the brief a pass receives is id, proposition and pin. Putting a prose digest into a record would mean the grounding pass reading the prose it exists to grade blind, which trades the independence the whole loop is built on for a residue line. The weaker one is genuinely constructible and was worked through rather than waved away: `render --out` could append a publication record \u2014 each prose block's text digest, each claim's proposition digest and whether anything grades it \u2014 and the residue would then be an ordinal comparison between successive publications with no clock in it at all. It is rejected on resolution, and the reason is structural too. A log that samples only when the author renders cannot order two events that fall inside one interval, and a grading followed by a prose edit followed by a single render is one interval. So a shipped-but-not-drift-covered snapshot file that changes what the report says is a category that already exists at this pin, with four members.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_refuted.json:103:   "text": "So the question becomes whether the digest-shaped alternative the ticket hoped for exists. Two were examined; both fail, and no claim is made that a third could not be found. The sharp one \u2014 a record carrying a digest of the prose it vouches for, the exact analogue of `out_of_proof` \u2014 cannot be built, for a structural reason rather than an oversight. `out_of_proof` compares digests because a record carries a digest of the very text it graded. No record names or digests a prose block anywhere in its shape, and the brief a pass receives is id, proposition and pin. Putting a prose digest into a record would mean the grounding pass reading the prose it exists to grade blind, which trades the independence the whole loop is built on for a residue line. The weaker one is genuinely constructible and was worked through rather than waved away: `render --out` could append a publication record \u2014 each prose block's text digest, each claim's proposition digest and whether anything grades it \u2014 and the residue would then be an ordinal comparison between successive publications with no clock in it at all. It is rejected on resolution, and the reason is structural too. A log that samples only when the author renders cannot order two events that fall inside one interval, and a grading followed by a prose edit followed by a single render is one interval. On the ticket's own account, that is the shape the finding took. The clock-free formulation would have been silent on it. That is the trade, stated plainly: the timestamp comparison buys the one ordering an interval-sampled log cannot, and pays for it with a bound it prints.",

/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_refuted.json:276:   "text": "The disclosure goes in the whole-search record's label, and it costs nothing in schema. TET-28 already added exactly one record per `look --grep` whose job is to say where a search started rather than what it hit \u2014 a `Search` entry when the grep matched, a `NoMatch` entry when it did not, and never both. That record is the natural and the only correct home for a statement about what the search did not visit, because the exclusion is a property of the search and not of any file it found. Putting the text there buys two carriers already built: the memo's Facts table renders each extent entry's label and renders nothing else from it, so the exclusion set is on the page for a reader who has only the committed document; and the pin hashes the label, so two searches with different exclusion sets fingerprint differently even when the text they matched is identical. It should also be printed in what `look` returns, for the author reading it in the moment \u2014 but the printed string is the convenience and the label is the record, which is the opposite of the two shapes this project has already been burned by: a warning with no lifecycle, and a refusal trail missing the refusal that mattered.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_refuted.json:445:   "text": "The ticket's sharpest question is whether the non-stationarity actually goes away, and the answer is no \u2014 it moves, and moving it is the point. Rendering a second memo into a scratch tree, touching no source, left the matched output of a search for the same symbol byte-identical while changing the exclusion list from one memo pattern to two. So the half the ticket complained about within a run is genuinely gone: an evidence ledger growing during grading cannot perturb a census any more, because the search never reaches it. But the exclusion set itself is a function of how many memos the tree holds, the design writes that set into the search record's label, and the label is inside the pin \u2014 so two censuses of one symbol against unchanged source will still pin differently either side of a render. That is not a leak that survived; it is the same fact about the world, moved out of the captured bytes where nobody could see it and into a sentence in the record where a reader comparing two pins is told immediately why they differ.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_refuted.json:458:   "text": "Nothing, and the answer has two halves, both of which can be shown rather than argued. The first is that the change cannot reach the check path at all: two exhaustive greps of the whole source tree find `Command::new` in only `observe.rs` \u2014 the grep inside `look_grep`, and `run_command`'s child \u2014 and `worldstate.rs`, where it runs git; and `observe::` in only `main.rs` and `mcp.rs`, which build a request and dispatch it, and `facts.rs`, where the single occurrence sits in a doc comment. Every other file in `src/` contains neither string, so nothing on the check or render path calls into the observe module or spawns a process. The second half is that there would be nothing to change even if it could: the `tetel fact` module states that extent, output and pin are set once at mint time and never appear in a revision event at all, so no code path exists that could rewrite them. The three committed memos keep the extents and pins they were minted with, whatever a `look` would do today.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_refuted.json:562:   "text": "The ticket asks whether the fix for the pin defect is to digest the pin or to compare it separately. Neither, and the reason splits by which record wrote the pin. On the witnessed path \u2014 the only one the floor counts \u2014 a record's pin is a content fingerprint over an observation's labels, world markers and output, while a claim's pin where it exists is a git short hash lifted from prose; the crate's own fixture ledger is where the operand does exist, both its claims pinned `abc1234`. Those two can never be equal, so the comparison fires on every claim always where a claim pin exists, and on none of the memos this tool renders, where no claim carries one. On the ingested path it is worse rather than better: the pin is copied straight from caller-supplied input with no shape check, so a reporter could type `abc1234` and discharge the comparison by typing \u2014 the same defect the floor sidesteps by counting witnessed records only. Under either reading the comparison carries no information about whether a wording has been graded.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_refuted.json:575:   "text": "The channel itself is not what the ticket supposed. Asked to confirm that a claim's pin moves only when its citation list moves, the code says otherwise: nothing derives a claim's pin from the facts it cites. The pin is read out of the prose \u2014 a sentence of the form \"at pin `<hash>`\" sitting between the nearest heading and the ledger table \u2014 and the single value found there is stamped onto every claim in that table. That parser is for imported, hand-authored ledgers; it finds nothing in a memo this tool rendered, which is the first half of why rule 3 needed rebuilding.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_refuted.json:865:   "text": "The ticket asks for four pieces to ship together, and it is worth being exact about the standing of each. One is measured: the replay's ordinal distribution and cost curve say what a floor of two buys and at what price. That is not the same as the figure the earlier draft of this memo led with \u2014 that a floor of one finds nothing \u2014 which follows from how a discovery is defined rather than from anything this ledger did. The closure and the visibility line are argued in this memo from what the code does, and nothing measures what their absence would cost. The fourth, pin-change detection, does not ship as a scheduling rule at all. /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_v1.json:119:   "text": "So the question becomes whether the digest-shaped alternative the ticket hoped for exists. Two were examined; both fail, and no claim is made that a third could not be found. The sharp one \u2014 a record carrying a digest of the prose it vouches for, the exact analogue of `out_of_proof` \u2014 cannot be built, for a structural reason rather than an oversight. `out_of_proof` compares digests because a record carries a digest of the very text it graded. No record names or digests a prose block anywhere in its shape, and the brief a pass receives is id, proposition and pin. Putting a prose digest into a record would mean the grounding pass reading the prose it exists to grade blind, which trades the independence the whole loop is built on for a residue line. The weaker one is genuinely constructible and was worked through rather than waved away: `render --out` could append a publication record \u2014 each prose block's text digest, each claim's proposition digest and whether anything grades it \u2014 and the residue would then be an ordinal comparison between successive publications with no clock in it at all. It is rejected on resolution, and the reason is structural too. A log that samples only when the author renders cannot order two events that fall inside one interval, and a grading followed by a prose edit followed by a single render is one interval. On the ticket's own account, that is the shape the finding took. The clock-free formulation would have been silent on it. That is the trade, stated plainly: the timestamp comparison buys the one ordering an interval-sampled log cannot, and pays for it with a bound it prints.",
