The reader who wants to re-take an observation should check that pin out first. Which tree each individual observation was actually taken against is not something this memo asserts \u2014 every observation carries its own working-tree marker, and `check` prints those states.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_v1.json:353:   "text": "The disclosure goes in the whole-search record's label, and it costs nothing in schema. TET-28 already added exactly one record per `look --grep` whose job is to say where a search started rather than what it hit \u2014 a `Search` entry when the grep matched, a `NoMatch` entry when it did not, and never both. That record is the natural and the only correct home for a statement about what the search did not visit, because the exclusion is a property of the search and not of any file it found. Putting the text there buys two carriers already built: the memo's Facts table renders each extent entry's label and renders nothing else from it, so the exclusion set is on the page for a reader who has only the committed document; and the pin hashes the label, so two searches with different exclusion sets fingerprint differently even when the text they matched is identical. It should also be printed in what `look` returns, for the author reading it in the moment \u2014 but the printed string is the convenience and the label is the record, which is the opposite of the two shapes this project has already been burned by: a warning with no lifecycle, and a refusal trail missing the refusal that mattered.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_v1.json:507:   "text": "The ticket's sharpest question is whether the non-stationarity actually goes away, and the answer is no \u2014 it moves, and moving it is the point. Rendering a second memo into a scratch tree, touching no source, left the matched output of a search for the same symbol byte-identical while changing the exclusion list from one memo pattern to two. So the half the ticket complained about within a run is genuinely gone: an evidence ledger growing during grading cannot perturb a census any more, because the search never reaches it. But the exclusion set itself is a function of how many memos the tree holds, the design writes that set into the search record's label, and the label is inside the pin \u2014 so two censuses of one symbol against unchanged source will still pin differently either side of a render. That is not a leak that survived; it is the same fact about the world, moved out of the captured bytes where nobody could see it and into a sentence in the record where a reader comparing two pins is told immediately why they differ.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_v1.json:518:   "text": "Nothing, and the answer has two halves, both of which can be shown rather than argued. The first is that the change cannot reach the check path at all: two exhaustive greps of the whole source tree find `Command::new` in only `observe.rs` \u2014 the grep inside `look_grep`, and `run_command`'s child \u2014 and `worldstate.rs`, where it runs git; and `observe::` in only `main.rs` and `mcp.rs`, which build a request and dispatch it, and `facts.rs`, where the single occurrence sits in a doc comment. Every other file in `src/` contains neither string, so nothing on the check or render path calls into the observe module or spawns a process. The second half is that there would be nothing to change even if it could: the `tetel fact` module states that extent, output and pin are set once at mint time and never appear in a revision event at all, so no code path exists that could rewrite them. The three committed memos keep the extents and pins they were minted with, whatever a `look` would do today.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_v1.json:617:   "text": "The ticket asks whether the fix for the pin defect is to digest the pin or to compare it separately. Neither, and the reason splits by which record wrote the pin. On the witnessed path \u2014 the only one the floor counts \u2014 a record's pin is a content fingerprint over an observation's labels, world markers and output, while a claim's pin where it exists is a git short hash lifted from prose; the crate's own fixture ledger is where the operand does exist, both its claims pinned `abc1234`. Those two can never be equal, so the comparison fires on every claim always where a claim pin exists, and on none of the memos this tool renders, where no claim carries one. On the ingested path it is worse rather than better: the pin is copied straight from caller-supplied input with no shape check, so a reporter could type `abc1234` and discharge the comparison by typing \u2014 the same defect the floor sidesteps by counting witnessed records only. Under either reading the comparison carries no information about whether a wording has been graded.",

/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_v1.json:981:   "text": "One asymmetry the design cannot close, and should not hide. Every figure in the replay counts gradings not performed, and a grading is not performed only if some pass declines to perform it. Nothing here makes that happen. A brief emits an id, a proposition, an optional pin and a withheld scope per claim, with no instruction prose in either renderer, and the invariant that keeps every claim in the list is the same one this design refused to touch. The owed section is therefore an artifact a pass may act on, not a mechanism that reduces what it grades. The costs on the other side are unconditional, and the largest of them was missing from an earlier draft: `brief_file` today reads a memo and renders it, calling neither `evidence::load` nor `analyze_ledger` and touching neither the snapshot path nor the workspace identity, so giving it the owed list turns it into a second ledger-analysis driver \u2014 a change of kind, not a threaded parameter. Add the floor through two front ends, a shape change to the JSON brief, and the widenings in the check path. The saving is real only if passes use the list, and no claim here says they will, because nothing in this repository could check it.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_v1.json:1051:   "text": "`look_grep` already does the two jobs separately. It runs grep once, then builds `printed` \u2014 the string handed back to the author, which today is grep's stdout verbatim followed by a parenthesised exclusion note \u2014 and, independently, the pending entries: one `Search` record carrying the root, the pattern and a matched-file count, and one `GrepMatch` record per matched file carrying that file's matched lines. The two are derived from the same stdout but neither reads the other, and that separation is what the bound rests on: out of a bounded call, every entry's captured output, its key and its world-tree markers come back byte-identical to what they are today, so two observations of one root still overlap and a later reader still re-reads the same bytes. What does not stay identical is the extent, the pin and the fact that ships. `facts::mint` copies each entry's label straight into the extent and hashes label, world markers and output into the pin, and this design writes a shortfall segment into the label \u2014 so wherever the bound bites, all three differ from what they would otherwise have been. That is the point and not a cost. It is the same property the exclusion note was given when TET-46 chose to list the skipped memo paths rather than count them, so that two searches withholding different things could not fingerprint alike; a bounded search and a whole one should not fingerprint alike either. What makes f3 cheap, and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope, is narrower than \"nothing changes\": no new record, no second pass over the buffer, nothing read back out of the entries, no signature touched. One number is computed while `printed` is being assembled, and the label is built from that number. The direction matters to whoever implements this \u2014 bound first, label from the bound. An implementer who bounds `printed` and leaves the label alone has rebuilt the silent cut this memo exists to remove.",
/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/scripts/verifier-eval/prose_v1.json:1120:   "text": "The other `look` path turns out to have a different answer from the one its shape suggests. `look_path` computes `shown` and uses it twice, but not as one value in one place: `printed` is a string of its own that receives a *copy* of `shown` by borrow, and only afterwards is `shown` moved into the pending entry's `output`. Two independent strings exist between those two points, so a bound applied to `printed` there leaves the captured output, the label, the key, the extent, the pin and the snapshot byte-identical \u2014 the same separation `look_grep` has, in a function that reads at first glance as though it has none. There is therefore no code-shaped reason to leave the plain `look <path>` alone, and no other reason either: a whole-file read that overruns the caller's cap is the same silent cut this design exists to stop. So it is bounded too, on the same terms.",

8668:     "The claim's own generalising argument does not stop where the claim stops it, and the standing line it specifies will mislead by contrast.

C15 argues correctly that a `NON_COVERAGE` line phrased about a search "would leave every bounded path read with no standing statement anywhere in the list, which is the one surface this design nominates for the general case", and concludes the line must say: "what `look` returned to its author is bounded, and a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed while nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it."

Run that argument one step further. `look` is not the only verb that writes an observation into the pending buffer and hands its author a return the caller then cuts. `run` does the same: `run_command` captures the child's merged stdout/stderr, pushes a `Proc` PendingEntry whose `output` is that capture, and returns it whole and unmeasured; both front ends hand it straight back with no size check — `print!("{}", outcome.printed)` at src/main.rs:526 and `"output": outcome.printed` at src/mcp.rs:653-656 (F3). The `run` tool's own description at src/mcp.rs:649 documents the large case explicitly ("a command whose output is enormous … puts that in a repository forever"). So a `run` observation has precisely the defect this design exists to remove — the coupling between what was captured and what the author saw is broken by the caller, silently — and after f3 it is not merely unfixed but affirmatively contrasted against, because the new standing line names `look`.

The condition C15 does not state: its second half — "a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed while nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it" — is true of every fact in the ledger regardless of which verb captured it, but the line as specified scopes it to `look`. A reader of `check`'s standing non-coverage will reasonably infer the caveat does not apply to `run`-captured facts, which is exactly backwards: those are the ones with no bound, no shortfall segment and no trace at all.

Not a demand that f3 bound `run` — that is a scoping decision the design may keep. What is owed is either a line whose general half is not verb-scoped, or a stated reason why `run` is excluded from a statement the design itself calls the general case."

15538:     "The claim's own generalising argument does not stop where the claim stops it, and the standing line it specifies will mislead by contrast.

C15 argues correctly that a `NON_COVERAGE` line phrased about a search "would leave every bounded path read with no standing statement anywhere in the list, which is the one surface this design nominates for the general case", and concludes the line must say: "what `look` returned to its author is bounded, and a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed while nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it."

Run that argument one step further. `look` is not the only verb that writes an observation into the pending buffer and hands its author a return the caller then cuts. `run` does the same: `run_command` captures the child's merged stdout/stderr, pushes a `Proc` PendingEntry whose `output` is that capture, and returns it whole and unmeasured; both front ends hand it straight back with no size check — `print!("{}", outcome.printed)` at src/main.rs:526 and `"output": outcome.printed` at src/mcp.rs:653-656 (F3). The `run` tool's own description at src/mcp.rs:649 documents the large case explicitly ("a command whose output is enormous … puts that in a repository forever"). So a `run` observation has precisely the defect this design exists to remove — the coupling between what was captured and what the author saw is broken by the caller, silently — and after f3 it is not merely unfixed but affirmatively contrasted against, because the new standing line names `look`.

The condition C15 does not state: its second half — "a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed while nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it" — is true of every fact in the ledger regardless of which verb captured it, but the line as specified scopes it to `look`. A reader of `check`'s standing non-coverage will reasonably infer the caveat does not apply to `run`-captured facts, which is exactly backwards: those are the ones with no bound, no shortfall segment and no trace at all.

Not a demand that f3 bound `run` — that is a scoping decision the design may keep. What is owed is either a line whose general half is not verb-scoped, or a stated reason why `run` is excluded from a statement the design itself calls the general case."

It reads exactly five things: that `kind` is Some(Search) or Some(NoMatch), that `pattern` byte-equals the symbol, that `world_root` is non-empty and not `worldstate::NO_GIT`, and that `key == world_root`. It never reads `label` and never reads `output`. Its doc comment states the predicate "is about existence and rooting, never about what was found".

(2) src/observe.rs lines 158-195, the head of `look_grep`. It refuses a non-existent root, then builds the argument vector: `-r` ONLY when `root_path.is_dir()`, then `-I`, `-n`, `-H`, `-e`, the pattern, and finally `root` — passed through verbatim as the caller spelled it, never canonicalized. `Command::new("grep")` is then invoked with that vector and the whole stdout is taken with `String::from_utf8_lossy`.",
1250:   "text": "TET-28's census refusal, in `targets::declare` (src/targets.rs:159-174), fires when no extent entry satisfies `ExtentEntry::censuses(symbol)`, and its own refusal text ends: "The refusal is about the search's existence and where it was rooted, never about what it found." The module doc (targets.rs:26-62) states the refusal makes "every declared target is censused" a workspace invariant because a fact's extent is immutable once minted, and that what declaration cannot reach is under-declaration — answered "by visibility instead", via the rendered section that does not disappear when empty and `check`'s standing non-coverage list.",

7647:     "True of the bound in isolation; false of the design, and the prose spends the unqualified form. `facts::mint` computes the pin as sha256 over, for every pending entry, `label` + `world_root` + `world_state` + `output` (facts.rs:417-435, its own comment: \"a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker\"), and copies `label` into the fact's extent (facts.rs:400-411). C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a \"showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)\" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes \u2014 the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests \"what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope\". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches \"would not pin identically\".\n\nThe second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries \"are built separately... neither reads the other\" \u2014 today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value (\"a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer\") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone \u2014 which is the design's own defect back again.\n\nWhat survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

710:   "prop": "A census check cannot be built on labels, and the record model already shows the right way to extend the schema. At mint time only key, label, world_root and world_state survive into an ExtentEntry \u2014 the observation's kind is dropped, and the grep pattern exists only inside a display label, where an author-chosen pattern containing \" in \" or \"(grep: \" would make parsing ambiguous. The census therefore needs the new root-level search entry to carry two structured fields into ExtentEntry \u2014 the observation kind and the search pattern \u2014 following the exact precedent world_root set: #[serde(default)], with the empty value read as \"predates the field, not eligible\" rather than guessed about. Legacy facts can then never satisfy a census requirement, whose remedy is precisely to re-run the grep under the new capture. The snapshot already ships facts.jsonl with full extent entries, so check reads these fields from files every snapshot already contains; and because no surface lets an author supply an extent by hand, both sides of the rooting comparison and the pattern are tool-captured by construction.",
714:     "Every checkable premise holds: ExtentEntry is exactly { key, label, world_root, world_state } and mint() copies only those four fields from PendingEntry, dropping kind; the pattern survives only inside the display labels (\"{file} (grep: {pattern})\", \"no-match: {pattern} in {root}\"), where a pattern containing \"(grep: \" or \" in \" is genuinely unparseable; world_root is #[serde(default)] with the empty value documented and treated as predating the field, comparable with nothing, rather than guessed about; the fact module states there is deliberately no surface to supply an extent by hand; and the snapshot ships facts.jsonl (first entry of SNAPSHOT_FILES) by verbatim copy, so the proposed fields would reach check in files every snapshot already contains."

14556:     "True of the bound in isolation; false of the design, and the prose spends the unqualified form. `facts::mint` computes the pin as sha256 over, for every pending entry, `label` + `world_root` + `world_state` + `output` (facts.rs:417-435, its own comment: \"a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker\"), and copies `label` into the fact's extent (facts.rs:400-411). C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a \"showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)\" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes \u2014 the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests \"what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope\". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches \"would not pin identically\".\n\nThe second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries \"are built separately... neither reads the other\" \u2014 today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value (\"a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer\") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone \u2014 which is the design's own defect back again.\n\nWhat survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

441:   "text": "The census predicate does not need to know, and should not be taught to. `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads five things \u2014 the record's kind, its pattern, that its world root is a real git root, and that the search key equals that root \u2014 and reads neither the label nor the output. It was always a predicate about a search's existence and where it started rather than about what the search saw, which is why a symbol with no occurrences is censused by the grep establishing it has none. That property is what lets this change through untouched: a worktree-rooted search is still a worktree-rooted search after it stops walking into snapshot directories. What moves is not the predicate but what a reader may conclude from one, and that is a matter of text in two places \u2014 a standing line in `check` saying the policy exists, and the search record's own label saying which exclusions this search was actually given.",
1256:   "text": "TET-28's refusal is untouched, and its wording needs no amendment. 5:    "prop": "A census check cannot be built on labels, and the record model already shows the right way to extend the schema. At mint time only key, label, world_root and world_state survive into an ExtentEntry \u2014 the observation's kind is dropped, and the grep pattern exists only inside a display label, where an author-chosen pattern containing \" in \" or \"(grep: \" would make parsing ambiguous. The census therefore needs the new root-level search entry to carry two structured fields into ExtentEntry \u2014 the observation kind and the search pattern \u2014 following the exact precedent world_root set: #[serde(default)], with the empty value read as \"predates the field, not eligible\" rather than guessed about. Legacy facts can then never satisfy a census requirement, whose remedy is precisely to re-run the grep under the new capture. The snapshot already ships facts.jsonl with full extent entries, so check reads these fields from files every snapshot already contains; and because no surface lets an author supply an extent by hand, both sides of the rooting comparison and the pattern are tool-captured by construction.",

4744:    "prop": "Containment against a fact's whole output has one genuine unsoundness, and it is fixable by the same schema move TET-28 already made. Fact.output is built at mint by joining the buffer entries' non-empty outputs with \"\\n\", and the per-entry boundaries are not stored \u2014 so \"substring of fact.output\" can be satisfied by text straddling the seam between two observations: bytes that were never contiguous in anything the author actually saw, e.g. the tail of one file's capture concatenated with the head of another's. The fix is a serde-defaulted per-entry field on ExtentEntry recording the entry's output byte length, mirroring exactly how kind and pattern were added for TET-28: boundaries become reconstructible from lengths (skipping zero-length entries, matching the mint-time filter), the premise relation is then \"verbatim substring of a single observation's output\", and a donor fact minted before the field existed is ineligible with the same remedy TET-28 gives legacy facts \u2014 re-look and re-mint. Absent means not recorded, never guessed.",

So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes \u2014 the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests \"what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope\". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches \"would not pin identically\".\n\nThe second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries \"are built separately... neither reads the other\" \u2014 today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value (\"a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer\") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone \u2014 which is the design's own defect back again.\n\nWhat survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

5:    "prop": "A census check cannot be built on labels, and the record model already shows the right way to extend the schema. At mint time only key, label, world_root and world_state survive into an ExtentEntry \u2014 the observation's kind is dropped, and the grep pattern exists only inside a display label, where an author-chosen pattern containing \" in \" or \"(grep: \" would make parsing ambiguous. The census therefore needs the new root-level search entry to carry two structured fields into ExtentEntry \u2014 the observation kind and the search pattern \u2014 following the exact precedent world_root set: #[serde(default)], with the empty value read as \"predates the field, not eligible\" rather than guessed about. Legacy facts can then never satisfy a census requirement, whose remedy is precisely to re-run the grep under the new capture. The snapshot already ships facts.jsonl with full extent entries, so check reads these fields from files every snapshot already contains; and because no surface lets an author supply an extent by hand, both sides of the rooting comparison and the pattern are tool-captured by construction.",

A census check cannot be built on labels, and the record model already shows the right way to extend the schema. At mint time only key, label, world_root and world_state survive into an ExtentEntry — the observation's kind is dropped, and the grep pattern exists only inside a display label, where an author-chosen pattern containing " in " or "(grep: " would make parsing ambiguous. The census therefore needs the new root-level search entry to carry two structured fields into ExtentEntry — the observation kind and the search pattern — following the exact precedent world_root set: #[serde(default)], with the empty value read as "predates the field, not eligible" rather than guessed about. Legacy facts can then never satisfy a census requirement, whose remedy is precisely to re-run the grep under the new capture. The snapshot already ships facts.jsonl with full extent entries, so check reads these fields from files every snapshot already contains; and because no surface lets an author supply an extent by hand, both sides of the rooting comparison and the pattern are tool-captured by construction.

380:   "text": "This design ran into its own subject before it could declare a single modification target, and the shape of that is worth stating rather than working around quietly. TET-28 requires a symbol an implementer is told to modify to be censused by a grep of the whole worktree. Every candidate symbol here was priced first: `look_grep` costs 709,469 bytes, `NON_COVERAGE` 858,096, `censuses` 691,562, `look_path` 688,776, `search_key` 633,291. The interesting number is not any one of them but the floor they share \u2014 roughly 0.63 MB is returned whichever symbol is asked for, because it is not about the symbol at all. Dropping snapshot directories and evidence ledgers alone removes between 95.9% and 99.9% of each. So the census requirement is today priced by tetel's own accumulated output rather than by the code being censused: two thirds of a megabyte comes back from grep, and is stored in the fact, per declared target.",

(a) src/observe.rs:342-412 `look_path`: the key is `resolve_key(p)` and the world marker is `worldstate::Session::new().for_path(p)` — both derived from the observed file, so an entry's `world_root` is the repository *the observed file lives in*, not the repository the caller was working in. (b) src/observe.rs:35-42 `resolve_key` falls back infallibly to `path.display()` when `fs::canonicalize` fails, so the key is NOT absolute by construction. src/observe.rs:56-67 `search_key` returns `world_root`'s own spelling when the search root and the world root canonicalize to the same directory.

text:
Constructed and captured on the release build at target/release/tetel: the symlink-into-a-different-repository case that defeats the key-derived rule anchored to the entry's own world_root.

Fixture: `outer/` is a git repository holding `README.md` and `x.txt` (contents "OUTER x"); `otherrepo/` is a separate git repository holding `x.txt` (contents "OTHER FILE"); `outer/link` is a committed symlink to `otherrepo`. `git -C outer rev-parse --show-toplevel` answers `.../outer`; the same command run inside `outer/link` answers `.../otherrepo`.

Attack: `tetel look .../outer/link/x.txt` mints an entry with key `.../otherrepo/x.txt`, label `.../outer/link/x.txt`, world_root `.../otherrepo`. The key is strictly under that entry's own world_root, so a rule that strips world_root from the key mints the relative label `x.txt` — not a refusal and not absolute. Rendered in a memo shipping in `outer`, `x.txt` resolves to `outer/x.txt`, a file that exists and holds "OUTER x" against the observed "OTHER FILE". This is silently-wrong, and it is reached with an ordinary symlink rather than a nested or vendored checkout.

Discriminator, captured: on the same build the caller's own spelling and the entry's world_root disagree here — the label `.../outer/link/x.txt` does not begin with world_root `.../otherrepo`. In the control observation, `tetel look .../outer/README.md`, key, label and world_root all agree: key and label are both `.../outer/README.md` and world_root is `.../outer`, so the spelling does begin with world_root. So requiring the caller's spelling to lie under the same world_root the key is relativized against separates the two cases on evidence available at capture, with no new tool invoked.

src/worldstate.rs:195-204 `Session::for_path` is why: it takes the containing directory and `fs::canonicalize`s it before asking git, so a path reached through a symlink is attributed to the tree the symlink points into, never to the tree the caller navigated from.

text: Whole-worktree census of `tree_report`, the symbol this design now tells an implementer to modify so that `check` reports which worktree root(s) a memo's relative labels are anchored to. In source it is defined at src/worldstate.rs:249, returns `TreeReport` (src/worldstate.rs:225), and is called from exactly one place, src/lib.rs:175, inside the check driver; its own module tests exercise it at src/worldstate.rs:322-376. Every other occurrence across the worktree is committed memo prose or a verifier-eval evaluation transcript under scripts/verifier-eval/. Nothing between a caller's argv and the stored label absolutizes a relative spelling. Constructed and captured on the release build: with the working directory in no repository at all, `look ../outer/x.txt` mints a key strictly under `outer`'s own root and a `world_root` that is that real repository — two of the three conditions — and stores the label `../outer/x.txt`. It lands in the "otherwise" branch and is relative, anchored to a working directory no reader of the memo has. Run from inside that repository, `look x.txt` stores `x.txt`, which is character-for-character what the root-relative rule would have minted. Two things follow. The caller-spelling condition has to say what a relative spelling is measured against, and the answer this design takes is a lexical join onto the process's working directory with no symlink resolution: both fixture arms then resolve under their own `world_root` and are relativized properly, while the symlink into another repository is refused exactly as before, its spelling being absolute already and outside the answering root. And the residue that still fails the condition cannot be promised absolute without a rewrite this ticket does not take on. The only absolutization on offer is a join onto the *process's* directory — what `fn resolved` does for the MCP handlers that call it, over a doc comment saying the server cannot know the caller's working directory — so keeping the promise would mean storing a path anchored to a directory the caller never chose and the memo never names, trading one unresolvable label for another. It would also rewrite labels for observations this design otherwise leaves alone, every relative-spelled `look` including the two CLI pin tests, and move their pins for a reason that has nothing to do with root-relativization. So the promise is dropped and the case is carried as a named risk instead, with the marker rather than the shape of the string as what distinguishes a root-relative label from a caller's own relative one — and, since the marker does not render, with `check` naming relative labels that carry none.

An absolute spelling is the literal string the caller typed. A relative spelling is the process's *physical* working directory — `std::env::current_dir()`, the getcwd(3) the operating system reports, in which the kernel has already resolved every symlink — and that string concatenated with a single separator between them: nothing is collapsed, no symlink is followed, no filesystem call is made. The first is closed at capture by requiring the caller's spelling and the key to agree on one root. The other two are not closed, only surfaced, by the check-time report of the distinct roots a memo's labels are anchored to — a report that tells a reader something is wrong without telling them which label is the wrong one. Neither shape occurs in this repository today.   look_grep:     709,469 bytes  ->   7,990 bytes
  NON_COVERAGE:  858,096 bytes  ->  34,595 bytes
  censuses:      691,562 bytes  ->   9,212 bytes
  look_path:     688,776 bytes  ->   8,132 bytes
  search_key:    633,291 bytes  ->     931 bytes

Every candidate census costs between 0.63 MB and 0.86 MB today, and two static exclusions remove between 95.9% and 99.9% of it. The floor of roughly 0.63 MB is shared across all five patterns, which is what tetel's own output contributes independently of which symbol is sought.",

It takes a single `path`, refuses if the path does not exist, refuses if the path is a directory (with the message "`tetel look` opens files. Use `tetel look --grep <pattern> {path}` to search it."), and otherwise reads exactly that one file with `fs::read_to_string`. There is no traversal of any kind in this function: it opens the file the caller named and nothing else. So every file `look_path` can ever return is a file the caller named explicitly.",
1123:   "text": "`look_path` (src/observe.rs:277-337) computes one value `shown` and uses it twice: it is pushed into `printed` after the `==> path <==` header, and it is moved into the `PendingEntry`'s `output`. Return and capture are the same bytes here, unlike `look_grep`. Its label already records a clamp against what was asked: `--lines a:b` with `b` past the end of file yields `format!("{path} lines {a}-{end}")` with `end = b.min(total)`, and a range entirely past the end yields `format!("{path} lines {a}-{b} (file has {total} line(s); nothing in range)")` with an empty `shown` — the doc comment calls this the same "a bounded negative must leave a trace" discipline as a zero-match grep.",
1224:   "text": "Contrary to the reading that return and capture are one value in `look_path`: at src/observe.rs:314-330 `printed` is a distinct `String::new()` that receives a COPY of `shown` via `printed.push_str(&shown)` (a borrow), and only afterwards is `shown` MOVED into `PendingEntry { output: shown, .. }`. Between the push_str and the move there are two independent strings, so a bound applied to `printed` at that point cannot reach `entry.output`, the entry's `label`, its `key`, its `world_root`/`world_state`, or anything that ships into the snapshot. Whatever `look_path` captures is byte-identical whether or not `printed` was bounded. The `label` computed at 297-312 is likewise built from `contents`/`lines`, never from `printed`.",
1260:   "text": "Whole-worktree census of `look_path` across /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel: four occurrences in one source file — the definition at src/observe.rs:277, the single call site inside `dispatch` at src/observe.rs:516, and two doc-comment mentions (observe.rs:4, observe.rs:495). No test, no binary and no other module names it, so a change confined to the function body touches nothing else. Same exclusions as this memo's other censuses (tetel's own output and git-ignored paths), and this run skipped seven rendered memos because this memo now exists among them.",
1361:   "text": "Two things that together make the zero-content case reachable and make a `look_path` shortfall recomputable from shipped bytes. (1) `look_path` (src/observe.rs:277-300) refuses exactly two conditions — a path that does not exist, and a directory — and then does `fs::read_to_string(p)` on whatever remains. No exclusion filtering is applied on this path at all: the only construction of `Exclusions` in the module is `Exclusions::decide(root_path)` at observe.rs:389, inside `look_grep`, and `decide` itself returns `Exclusions::None { why: "the caller named one file" }` for any root that is not a directory. So a tracked path under a `.tetel/` snapshot directory is opened by `look <path>` like any other file, and the four long-line ledgers are reachable. (2) `snapshot.rs`'s `SNAPSHOT_FILES` (src/snapshot.rs:71-100) is a ten-entry enumeration whose first element is `facts.jsonl`, so every fact's persisted `output` — for a `Path` entry, the complete selected text — ships beside the rendered memo. The enumeration's own comment says the list is enumerated rather than copied wholesale so that shipping a workspace file is a deliberate decision.",
1385:   "text": "What `look_path` selects and what it wraps that selection in, read at src/observe.rs:277-337 for the purpose of settling the budget's referent on the path side. (1) The selected text is `shown`: with no `--lines` it is `contents.clone()`, the whole file; with `--lines a:b` it is `all[a - 1..end].join("\n")` over `contents.lines()`, where `end = b.min(total)` — so the selection is 1-based, begins at line `a`, and is joined without a trailing newline. (2) `printed` is a separate `String::new()` assembled in up to three pushes: `printed.push_str(&format!("==> {path} <==\n"))`, then `printed.push_str(&shown)`, then a single `'\n'` if `shown` is non-empty and does not already end in one. (3) The header therefore exists in `printed` and in no other place: `PendingEntry { output: shown, .. }` receives the selection alone, so neither the header nor the trailing-newline pad is ever part of the captured output, the label, the key or anything that ships in the snapshot. A budget measured over the assembled `printed` would consume the header before any content, and would count `==> ` plus the path plus ` <==\n` against the file's own bytes; a budget measured over `shown` counts only what was selected.",
1450:   "text": "In `look_path` the label is finished before the string the bound applies to exists — the opposite statement order from `look_grep`. `let (shown, label) = match lines { ... };` completes at observe.rs:297-312 and fixes `label` in all three of its arms (`path.to_string()`, the "nothing in range" form, and `{path} lines {a}-{end}`), and only afterwards, at observe.rs:314, does `let mut printed = String::new()` begin assembling the return. The label is then moved into `PendingEntry { label, .. }` at 321-330 unchanged. So an implementer who bounds `printed` at 316 where `shown` is pushed, and leaves the `match lines` block untouched, gets a cut return with a label that says nothing about the cut, which is the silent cut the design exists to stop. In `look_grep` the same edit is naturally safe: `printed.push_str(&stdout)` at observe.rs:438 opens the match branch and the `Search` label is built afterwards at 457-460.",

2948:   "prop": "\"No `look` returns tetel's own content\" is not the honest name for what this design builds, and the honest name is better rather than merely narrower: a `look` returns tetel's own output only when the caller named it. `look_path` refuses a directory and reads exactly the one file it was given, with no traversal of any kind, so every file it can ever return is one the caller named explicitly and it is left unchanged by this design. `look_grep` is where the whole mechanism lands, and its rule is the same sentence applied to a search \u2014 the exclusions are passed only when the root is a directory that is not itself tetel content, so what they remove is only ever reached by traversal. 3050:   "prop": "No opt-out flag should be added, because three escape hatches already exist and each is reached by naming something rather than by setting a flag. `look_path` opens any single named file, including one inside a snapshot, and is untouched by this design. `look --grep` rooted at a path that is itself tetel content passes no exclusions at all, which is not merely permitted but forced: grep's `--exclude-dir` suppresses a directory named as the recursion root, so the flags must be withheld there or naming a snapshot directory would return nothing. And `run` spawns `argv` directly with nothing between the empty-argv refusal and the spawn that inspects, parses or classifies the command or the paths it will touch, so it has no place a path exclusion could be applied even in principle. A flag would add a fourth route that, unlike all three of these, leaves no trace in what was named.",

7647:     "True of the bound in isolation; false of the design, and the prose spends the unqualified form. `facts::mint` computes the pin as sha256 over, for every pending entry, `label` + `world_root` + `world_state` + `output` (facts.rs:417-435, its own comment: \"a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker\"), and copies `label` into the fact's extent (facts.rs:400-411). C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a \"showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)\" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes \u2014 the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests \"what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope\". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches \"would not pin identically\".\n\nThe second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries \"are built separately... neither reads the other\" \u2014 today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value (\"a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer\") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone \u2014 which is the design's own defect back again.\n\nWhat survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

7893:     "The reason given is sound \u2014 a mid-line cut does hand the author a fragment that is not a match record \u2014 but the rule the design derives from it (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\") has no floor, and with C8's 32768 it admits a return of zero content whenever the first candidate line exceeds the budget. That state is reachable here, not hypothetical: F1(7) finds four tracked files in this worktree with a single line over 32768 bytes (up to 905745), and F1(4) confirms `look_path` filters nothing, so any of them can be opened directly. The claim as written establishes only that the cut must fall on a line boundary; it does not establish that a line-boundary cut always returns something, and the design nowhere states what happens when it returns nothing. Either state the floor (admit at least one line, cutting it mid-line and saying so) or state explicitly that a line longer than the budget is unreturnable \u2014 the current wording leaves an implementer to discover the zero-byte case in production."
7897:     "Everything measurable here checks out: grep is run with -I -n -H so its output line is `<file>:<lineno>:<text>` and `look_grep` splits on `stdout.lines()`; exactly four tracked paths hold a single line over 32768 bytes, up to 905745, and all four are *.tetel/facts.jsonl snapshot ledgers (F3); a whole-`src` grep for `is_char_boundary`, `char_indices` and `.truncate(` returns no hits at all (F3); the longest single line carries 1922 UTF-8 continuation bytes (F6). The clause that does not hold as written is \"`look_path` refuses only a missing path and a directory\": `look_path` has a third refusal in its body, `invalid --lines range {a}:{b}` when `a < 1 || a > b` (observe.rs:300-302). 8228:   "prop": "The plain `look <path>` and `look --lines A:B` paths must be left alone by this design, because in `look_path` the returned bytes and the captured `output` are the same value `shown`; bounding the return there would necessarily change what is captured, which the ticket puts out of scope. `look_grep` is bounded and `look_path` is not, and that asymmetry is a consequence of the code's shape, not an oversight.",
8232:     "The claim's premise is right and its inference is false. In `look_path` (observe.rs 268-336) `printed` is a separate String assembled by `printed.push_str(&shown)` at line 316 \u2014 a byte copy \u2014 and `shown` is moved into `PendingEntry.output` afterwards at line 325. Two independent Strings exist between those points, which is the same separation `look_grep` exploits. Bounding `printed` after line 316 would therefore NOT \"necessarily change what is captured\": the capture would be byte-identical, exactly as C2 says it is on the grep path. So the asymmetry is not \"a consequence of the code's shape\"; it is a choice the design is entitled to make but has not justified. This matters because C9 is an instruction to an implementer \u2014 it tells them the `look <path>` case is closed by construction, which suppresses the observation that after f3 ships, `look <path>` on a large file is still silently cut by the caller with no trace anywhere, the very defect the ticket names."

8660:     "This claim instructs an implementer what a declared modification target (`NON_COVERAGE`) must say, and what it specifies is census-shaped while the design is not. Its content sentence is \"a fact's extent records the whole search, and nothing anywhere establishes that the author read all of it\", and the prose spends it the same way (\"the list carries the general statement that a census's return to its author is bounded\"), as does C16 (\"the static list says a census reports the tree minus what tetel withheld\"). But C9 and C20 put `look_path` inside the same bound, and F1(4) confirms a plain `look <path>` is a wholly different act \u2014 no search, no root, no exclusions, an extent naming one file and a range. An implementer who writes the line this claim specifies leaves every bounded path read with no standing statement anywhere in `check`'s non-coverage list, which is the one surface the design nominates for the general case. The single-line decision may well still be right, but the line has to be written for both acts \u2014 \"what `look` returns to its author is bounded, and nothing establishes the author read the whole of what the extent records\" \u2014 not for a census. As it stands the claim's own wording, followed literally, produces a line that covers `look_grep` only."
8664:     "report.rs:86-190 carries both entries and the comment between them verbatim: the platform-accident entry (\"symlinked directories and binary files\"), the tetel-output entry, and \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\". No entry in the list concerns what `look` returned to its author. `look_path` applying no exclusion filtering is F2 and is also stated in the tetel-output entry itself; scope.rs naming interpretation/insincere examination as permanently out of reach is F5."
8672:     "The verifiable parts hold. The standing list does discriminate a chosen withholding from platform accidents, and its comment says verbatim \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\", beside the entry naming grep skipping symlinked directories and binary files. The first half's factual load is correct: `run_command` returns the child's whole captured output unmeasured with no length test anywhere in the function, and both front ends hand it back whole (`print!(\"{}\", outcome.printed)` in main.rs's Run arm; `\"output\": outcome.printed` in the MCP run tool); the run tool's own description does contemplate \"a command whose output is enormous\" and answers by warning rather than bounding. `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering at all.\n\nThe qualification is the clause \"`scope.rs` names that second half as permanently out of reach\". The only occurrence of \"permanently out of reach\" in the whole of src/ is src/scope.rs:42, and what it registers there is a different proposition: \"Whether the note is *correct* about the location it names is exactly the limit this project registered as permanently out of reach (\\\"insincere examination\\\" \u2014 capture makes the extent honest, not the interpretation).\" That is about the truth of an author's interpretation of a location, not about how much of a capture the author was shown. Reading it as naming the second half (\"a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed, and nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it\") requires stretching \"insincere examination\" from not-examined to not-shown, and scope.rs does not spell that out. This matters because it is the clause carrying the memo's assurance that the new entry \"names an old limit that had been invisible rather than admitting a new weakness\" \u2014 after the bound, `look` genuinely shows the author less than the extent records, which is new. Separate, non-blocking: the list itself is `NON_COVERAGE` in src/report.rs:86, not in scope.rs; C15 does not misattribute it, but the two files are easy to conflate here."

Take `look /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/docs/design/tet46-look-never-returns-tetel-content.md.tetel/facts.jsonl`. F1(7) measures it: 20 lines, of which two exceed 32768 bytes, the longest 905745. F1(4) confirms `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering of any kind, so a named snapshot path is read like any other file \u2014 nothing stops this call. Under the rule the design states (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\", C5/C20), the return stops at whichever over-budget line comes first. The author then asks for the rest with `--lines k:20`. The selection now BEGINS with a 905745-byte line, no whole line fits under 32768, and the bound admits zero lines: the author gets the `==> path <==` header, an empty body, and a label reading \"showed 0 of N lines (32768-byte bound)\". Every range that includes that line behaves identically. There is no `--lines` argument that returns any byte of it, so the claim's remedy does not reach it, and \"needs nothing new either\" is false: this case needs something the design does not have (a floor of one line, a byte-level fallback for an over-budget line, or at minimum an explicit statement that an over-budget line is unreadable through `look`).\n\nWorse than the status quo on exactly the axis the ticket cares about. Today the caller truncates at ~59 KB, so the author reading that file sees its first ~59 KB. Under the design they see zero bytes of that line. The memo's answer to \"what does an author do\" is that the design \"does not give the author back what was withheld; it stops the withholding from being secret\" \u2014 but here the design withholds strictly more than the status quo did, and this claim asserts a remedy that does not exist.\n\nThe same construction reaches `look_grep`: a grep whose matching line is one of these long JSON lines emits a `<file>:<lineno>:<text>` line over the budget, and if it is the first matching line the bounded return is empty while the label still says \"N files matched\". The prose's consolation that \"even a heavily bounded return still tells the author truthfully how many files matched\" is then a file count attached to nothing."

8974:     "The exemption holds for the grep label and does not extend to the `look_path` label the revision brought inside the bound. Every reason this claim gives is grep-shaped: \"the `Search` entry's `output` is empty and the per-file entries record what was captured, not how much of it was returned\". For `look_path` neither is true. F1(4): the `Path` entry's `output` is `shown` \u2014 the complete selected text, in original order, moved in whole \u2014 and F1(6): facts.jsonl, carrying that output, ships into the snapshot. So for the `look_path` label required by C20, N is a pure function of shipped data and a documented constant: replay whole lines of the stored `output` until 32768 is passed and you have N. That is exactly the class the doctrine (F15/lib.rs:136-141) says to recompute rather than persist, and this claim's stated ground for the exemption \u2014 \"unrecoverable from the ledger after the fact\" \u2014 is false there. The conclusion may still be defensible for `look_path` on other grounds (an author-facing label is not a stored derivation to be recomputed by `check`), but the memo does not make that argument, and this claim's argument does not cover half of what the design writes the number into. Grep is untouched by this: the `Search` output is empty and `by_file` is a BTreeMap, so the stdout order the bound consumed is not recoverable from the per-file entries."
8982:     "The conclusion holds; the two-paths distinction the claim draws does not, on the mode axis. C19 says that for `look_grep` the number is \"plainly outside the rule\" because the per-file entries \"are keyed into a `BTreeMap` by filename, so the stdout order the bound consumed is not in the ledger and N is unrecoverable from it\", and reserves the two fallback grounds for `look_path`. `look_grep` is two instruments selected by one argument value: `-r` is pushed only `if root_path.is_dir()` (observe.rs:352-353) and `Exclusions::decide` returns `None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for a non-directory root, so `look --grep <pattern> <one file>` is a first-class mode, exercised at tests/authoring_cli.rs:473 and :485. In that mode `by_file` has exactly one key and its `Vec<String>` holds every matched line's `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order \u2014 the order the bound consumed \u2014 and the shipped `GrepMatch` entry carries that Vec joined by \"\\n\" as its `output` with `{file} (grep: {pattern})` as its label, so the `{file}:` prefix the bound counted is recoverable too. Full stdout is reconstructible byte-for-byte, and the design's own label states the budget it applied, so replaying the release rule reproduces N exactly. What C19 asserts is unrecoverable is recoverable in this mode. The claim's conclusion survives untouched, because the two grounds it states for `look_path` \u2014 that a replay answers what today's build would show rather than what this author was shown, and that a label's audience holds a rendered memo with no captured output in front of them \u2014 apply verbatim to a single-file grep. The narrowing owed is that the ledger-order argument covers only the recursive mode, and that both paths rest on the same two grounds wherever it does not."
8986:     "Read directly in src/observe.rs. Recursive mode: the Search entry's `output` is `String::new()`, and the per-file entries are collected into `by_file: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>` keyed by filename, so grep's stdout order \u2014 the order a bound would consume \u2014 is not in the ledger. Two instruments by one argument value: `args.push(\"-r\")` runs only inside `if root_path.is_dir()`, and `Exclusions::decide` (observe.rs:240-259) returns `Exclusions::None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for any non-directory root, verbatim. In single-file mode `-H` is pushed unconditionally so every line is `{file}:{lineno}:{text}` and `split_once(':')` yields one constant key, hence exactly one by_file entry whose Vec holds every matched line as `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order, shipped as `output: matches.join(\"\\n\")` under `label: format!(\"{file} (grep: {pattern})\")` \u2014 file, order and every matched line all in the ledger, so the full stdout reconstructs from that one entry. For look_path, `PendingEntry { output: shown, .. }` receives the complete selection."

2704:   "prop": "\"Transcribed verbatim\" cannot be an honour-system field, and does not need to be: the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output. Both sides of that comparison are Strings the tool controls \u2014 a fact's output is produced only by look/run (file bytes read verbatim by look_path, grep match lines, a process's merged stream), no authoring surface lets anyone supply output by hand, and output is immutable after mint \u2014 so substring containment is a pure byte-level comparison with no normalisation step owned by the check. Typing is the selection mechanism, not the trust: the author types the premise, but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb. This is exactly the README's Direction item for supporting-span selection (\"refused unless it is a verbatim substring of a cited fact \u2014 the author cannot type an extent, and here could not invent support, only select it\"), and TET-29 is the first place it becomes load-bearing rather than roadmap.",

2926:   "prop": "The strictness objections to byte-level containment dissolve on the actual capture path, and every weaker relation reopens the invention channel. A donor comment wrapped across lines with interior prefix noise (`//`, `*`, indentation) IS a contiguous byte substring of a look_path capture, because look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim \u2014 the cost is only that the selected premise carries its comment syntax into the rendered section, which the \"never paraphrase\" constraint endorses rather than tolerates. Stripping that noise would require knowing each language's comment syntax, which is precisely the hard-coded per-language coupling scope.rs's \"language-agnostic by construction\" doctrine excludes. Two capture modes genuinely fight containment \u2014 grep-derived match outputs interleave \"lineno:\" prefixes between lines, and whole-search/no-match records carry empty output \u2014 so the design's guidance is that a donor fact is minted from `look` of the donor file; that is guidance about which observation to select from, not a new rule, since the relation is indifferent to which kind produced the bytes. Weaker relations fail: per-line containment lets an author stitch non-adjacent lines into a sentence the donor never wrote, and whitespace- or case-normalised matching means the memo shows text the capture does not contain \u2014 both are paraphrase with extra steps.",
2930:     "The capture-path clauses check out with one unstated condition. Grep-derived per-file outputs do carry \"lineno:\" prefixes on every line, and both Search and NoMatch records store empty output \u2014 verified in look_grep. But \"look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim\" is unconditionally true only for the plain open: with --lines, look_path collects contents.lines() and re-joins with \"\\n\", which reproduces the file's bytes for LF files but not for CRLF files (and read_to_string refuses non-UTF-8 entirely). A wrapped donor comment is a contiguous substring of a whole-file capture; for a --lines capture that holds only under the LF condition the proposition does not state."
2938:     "Each capture-mode assertion is what observe.rs does: plain look_path stores fs::read_to_string's contents verbatim (no normalisation); --lines stores all[a-1..end].join(\"\\n\"), and Rust's lines() strips \\r on CRLF and the final join drops the trailing newline \u2014 in that mode only, exactly as claimed. So a multi-line prefixed comment is a contiguous substring of the capture in both modes. The two fighting modes are real too: per-file grep entries join \"lineno:\"-prefixed match lines, and the Search/NoMatch whole-search records carry output: String::new(). The stitching argument against per-line containment follows directly from the \"\\n\"-join."

3054:   "prop": "The strictness objections to byte-level containment dissolve on the actual capture path, and every weaker relation reopens the invention channel. A donor comment wrapped across lines with interior prefix noise (`//`, `*`, indentation) IS a contiguous byte substring of a look_path capture, because look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim \u2014 the cost is only that the selected premise carries its comment syntax into the rendered section, which the \"never paraphrase\" constraint endorses rather than tolerates. Stripping that noise would require knowing each language's comment syntax, which is precisely the hard-coded per-language coupling scope.rs's \"language-agnostic by construction\" doctrine excludes. Two capture modes genuinely fight containment \u2014 grep-derived match outputs interleave \"lineno:\" prefixes between lines, and whole-search/no-match records carry empty output \u2014 so the design's guidance is that a donor fact is minted from `look` of the donor file; that is guidance about which observation to select from, not a new rule, since the relation is indifferent to which kind produced the bytes. Weaker relations fail: per-line containment lets an author stitch non-adjacent lines into a sentence the donor never wrote, and whitespace- or case-normalised matching means the memo shows text the capture does not contain \u2014 both are paraphrase with extra steps.",
3058:     "The capture-path clauses check out with one unstated condition. Grep-derived per-file outputs do carry \"lineno:\" prefixes on every line, and both Search and NoMatch records store empty output \u2014 verified in look_grep. But \"look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim\" is unconditionally true only for the plain open: with --lines, look_path collects contents.lines() and re-joins with \"\\n\", which reproduces the file's bytes for LF files but not for CRLF files (and read_to_string refuses non-UTF-8 entirely). A wrapped donor comment is a contiguous substring of a whole-file capture; for a --lines capture that holds only under the LF condition the proposition does not state."
3066:     "Each capture-mode assertion is what observe.rs does: plain look_path stores fs::read_to_string's contents verbatim (no normalisation); --lines stores all[a-1..end].join(\"\\n\"), and Rust's lines() strips \\r on CRLF and the final join drops the trailing newline \u2014 in that mode only, exactly as claimed. So a multi-line prefixed comment is a contiguous substring of the capture in both modes. The two fighting modes are real too: per-file grep entries join \"lineno:\"-prefixed match lines, and the Search/NoMatch whole-search records carry output: String::new(). The stitching argument against per-line containment follows directly from the \"\\n\"-join."

9312:   "prop": "\"No `look` returns tetel's own content\" is not the honest name for what this design builds, and the honest name is better rather than merely narrower: a `look` returns tetel's own output only when the caller named it. `look_path` refuses a directory and reads exactly the one file it was given, with no traversal of any kind, so every file it can ever return is one the caller named explicitly and it is left unchanged by this design. `look_grep` is where the whole mechanism lands, and its rule is the same sentence applied to a search \u2014 the exclusions are passed only when the root is a directory that is not itself tetel content, so what they remove is only ever reached by traversal. 9411:   "prop": "No opt-out flag should be added, because three escape hatches already exist and each is reached by naming something rather than by setting a flag. `look_path` opens any single named file, including one inside a snapshot, and is untouched by this design. `look --grep` rooted at a path that is itself tetel content passes no exclusions at all, which is not merely permitted but forced: grep's `--exclude-dir` suppresses a directory named as the recursion root, so the flags must be withheld there or naming a snapshot directory would return nothing. And `run` spawns `argv` directly with nothing between the empty-argv refusal and the spawn that inspects, parses or classifies the command or the paths it will touch, so it has no place a path exclusion could be applied even in principle. A flag would add a fourth route that, unlike all three of these, leaves no trace in what was named.",
9415:     "Escape hatches 1 and 3: look_path opens any single named file with no traversal and nothing in this design touches it; run_command has only the empty-argv refusal between entry and `Command::new(&argv[0]).spawn()`, with no inspection of the command or its paths, so it offers no place to apply an exclusion."

14556:     "True of the bound in isolation; false of the design, and the prose spends the unqualified form. `facts::mint` computes the pin as sha256 over, for every pending entry, `label` + `world_root` + `world_state` + `output` (facts.rs:417-435, its own comment: \"a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker\"), and copies `label` into the fact's extent (facts.rs:400-411). C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a \"showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)\" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes \u2014 the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests \"what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope\". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches \"would not pin identically\".\n\nThe second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries \"are built separately... neither reads the other\" \u2014 today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value (\"a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer\") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone \u2014 which is the design's own defect back again.\n\nWhat survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

14793:     "The reason given is sound \u2014 a mid-line cut does hand the author a fragment that is not a match record \u2014 but the rule the design derives from it (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\") has no floor, and with C8's 32768 it admits a return of zero content whenever the first candidate line exceeds the budget. 15109:   "prop": "The plain `look <path>` and `look --lines A:B` paths must be left alone by this design, because in `look_path` the returned bytes and the captured `output` are the same value `shown`; bounding the return there would necessarily change what is captured, which the ticket puts out of scope. `look_grep` is bounded and `look_path` is not, and that asymmetry is a consequence of the code's shape, not an oversight.",
15113:     "The claim's premise is right and its inference is false. In `look_path` (observe.rs 268-336) `printed` is a separate String assembled by `printed.push_str(&shown)` at line 316 \u2014 a byte copy \u2014 and `shown` is moved into `PendingEntry.output` afterwards at line 325. Two independent Strings exist between those points, which is the same separation `look_grep` exploits. Bounding `printed` after line 316 would therefore NOT \"necessarily change what is captured\": the capture would be byte-identical, exactly as C2 says it is on the grep path. So the asymmetry is not \"a consequence of the code's shape\"; it is a choice the design is entitled to make but has not justified. This matters because C9 is an instruction to an implementer \u2014 it tells them the `look <path>` case is closed by construction, which suppresses the observation that after f3 ships, `look <path>` on a large file is still silently cut by the caller with no trace anywhere, the very defect the ticket names."

15530:     "This claim instructs an implementer what a declared modification target (`NON_COVERAGE`) must say, and what it specifies is census-shaped while the design is not. Its content sentence is \"a fact's extent records the whole search, and nothing anywhere establishes that the author read all of it\", and the prose spends it the same way (\"the list carries the general statement that a census's return to its author is bounded\"), as does C16 (\"the static list says a census reports the tree minus what tetel withheld\"). But C9 and C20 put `look_path` inside the same bound, and F1(4) confirms a plain `look <path>` is a wholly different act \u2014 no search, no root, no exclusions, an extent naming one file and a range. An implementer who writes the line this claim specifies leaves every bounded path read with no standing statement anywhere in `check`'s non-coverage list, which is the one surface the design nominates for the general case. The single-line decision may well still be right, but the line has to be written for both acts \u2014 \"what `look` returns to its author is bounded, and nothing establishes the author read the whole of what the extent records\" \u2014 not for a census. As it stands the claim's own wording, followed literally, produces a line that covers `look_grep` only."
15534:     "report.rs:86-190 carries both entries and the comment between them verbatim: the platform-accident entry (\"symlinked directories and binary files\"), the tetel-output entry, and \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\". No entry in the list concerns what `look` returned to its author. `look_path` applying no exclusion filtering is F2 and is also stated in the tetel-output entry itself; scope.rs naming interpretation/insincere examination as permanently out of reach is F5."
15542:     "The verifiable parts hold. The standing list does discriminate a chosen withholding from platform accidents, and its comment says verbatim \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\", beside the entry naming grep skipping symlinked directories and binary files. The first half's factual load is correct: `run_command` returns the child's whole captured output unmeasured with no length test anywhere in the function, and both front ends hand it back whole (`print!(\"{}\", outcome.printed)` in main.rs's Run arm; `\"output\": outcome.printed` in the MCP run tool); the run tool's own description does contemplate \"a command whose output is enormous\" and answers by warning rather than bounding. `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering at all.\n\nThe qualification is the clause \"`scope.rs` names that second half as permanently out of reach\". The only occurrence of \"permanently out of reach\" in the whole of src/ is src/scope.rs:42, and what it registers there is a different proposition: \"Whether the note is *correct* about the location it names is exactly the limit this project registered as permanently out of reach (\\\"insincere examination\\\" \u2014 capture makes the extent honest, not the interpretation).\" That is about the truth of an author's interpretation of a location, not about how much of a capture the author was shown. Reading it as naming the second half (\"a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed, and nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it\") requires stretching \"insincere examination\" from not-examined to not-shown, and scope.rs does not spell that out. This matters because it is the clause carrying the memo's assurance that the new entry \"names an old limit that had been invisible rather than admitting a new weakness\" \u2014 after the bound, `look` genuinely shows the author less than the extent records, which is new. Separate, non-blocking: the list itself is `NON_COVERAGE` in src/report.rs:86, not in scope.rs; C15 does not misattribute it, but the two files are easy to conflate here."

15624:     "The verifiable parts hold. The standing list does discriminate a chosen withholding from platform accidents, and its comment says verbatim \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\", beside the entry naming grep skipping symlinked directories and binary files. The first half's factual load is correct: `run_command` returns the child's whole captured output unmeasured with no length test anywhere in the function, and both front ends hand it back whole (`print!(\"{}\", outcome.printed)` in main.rs's Run arm; `\"output\": outcome.printed` in the MCP run tool); the run tool's own description does contemplate \"a command whose output is enormous\" and answers by warning rather than bounding. `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering at all.\n\nThe qualification is the clause \"`scope.rs` names that second half as permanently out of reach\". The only occurrence of \"permanently out of reach\" in the whole of src/ is src/scope.rs:42, and what it registers there is a different proposition: \"Whether the note is *correct* about the location it names is exactly the limit this project registered as permanently out of reach (\\\"insincere examination\\\" \u2014 capture makes the extent honest, not the interpretation).\" That is about the truth of an author's interpretation of a location, not about how much of a capture the author was shown. Reading it as naming the second half (\"a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed, and nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it\") requires stretching \"insincere examination\" from not-examined to not-shown, and scope.rs does not spell that out. This matters because it is the clause carrying the memo's assurance that the new entry \"names an old limit that had been invisible rather than admitting a new weakness\" \u2014 after the bound, `look` genuinely shows the author less than the extent records, which is new. Separate, non-blocking: the list itself is `NON_COVERAGE` in src/report.rs:86, not in scope.rs; C15 does not misattribute it, but the two files are easy to conflate here."
15724:     "The numbers and the unit are confirmed independently (F6): reproducing look_grep's own exclusion set and running the grep gives exactly 883 matching lines and 70 distinct first-colon fields, and appending one trailing parenthesised exclusion-note line raises the distinct-field count to 71, which is the stated cause of the earlier figure. `by_file.len()` is indeed the count of distinct first-colon fields and is computed from the full stdout (F2), and `stdout.lines()` is what look_grep splits on. The clause that does not hold as written is the closing analogy, \"which is how `look --lines` already annotates a range only when it was clamped\": look_path writes `{path} lines {a}-{end}` into the label on every ranged read, clamped or not (observe.rs:308-309), so the range annotation is not clamp-conditional.
