15868:     "The `look_path` half of this claim \u2014 \"`--lines A:B` is already a first-class parameter of the same verb, so the author reads the rest of the file by asking for it\" \u2014 is broken by a state reachable on tracked files in this worktree.\n\nConstruction. Take `look /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/docs/design/tet46-look-never-returns-tetel-content.md.tetel/facts.jsonl`. F1(7) measures it: 20 lines, of which two exceed 32768 bytes, the longest 905745. F1(4) confirms `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering of any kind, so a named snapshot path is read like any other file \u2014 nothing stops this call. Under the rule the design states (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\", C5/C20), the return stops at whichever over-budget line comes first. The author then asks for the rest with `--lines k:20`. The selection now BEGINS with a 905745-byte line, no whole line fits under 32768, and the bound admits zero lines: the author gets the `==> path <==` header, an empty body, and a label reading \"showed 0 of N lines (32768-byte bound)\". Every range that includes that line behaves identically. There is no `--lines` argument that returns any byte of it, so the claim's remedy does not reach it, and \"needs nothing new either\" is false: this case needs something the design does not have (a floor of one line, a byte-level fallback for an over-budget line, or at minimum an explicit statement that an over-budget line is unreadable through `look`).\n\nWorse than the status quo on exactly the axis the ticket cares about. Today the caller truncates at ~59 KB, so the author reading that file sees its first ~59 KB. Under the design they see zero bytes of that line. The memo's answer to \"what does an author do\" is that the design \"does not give the author back what was withheld; it stops the withholding from being secret\" \u2014 but here the design withholds strictly more than the status quo did, and this claim asserts a remedy that does not exist.\n\nThe same construction reaches `look_grep`: a grep whose matching line is one of these long JSON lines emits a `<file>:<lineno>:<text>` line over the budget, and if it is the first matching line the bounded return is empty while the label still says \"N files matched\". The prose's consolation that \"even a heavily bounded return still tells the author truthfully how many files matched\" is then a file count attached to nothing."

15979:     "The exemption holds for the grep label and does not extend to the `look_path` label the revision brought inside the bound. Every reason this claim gives is grep-shaped: \"the `Search` entry's `output` is empty and the per-file entries record what was captured, not how much of it was returned\". For `look_path` neither is true. F1(4): the `Path` entry's `output` is `shown` \u2014 the complete selected text, in original order, moved in whole \u2014 and F1(6): facts.jsonl, carrying that output, ships into the snapshot. So for the `look_path` label required by C20, N is a pure function of shipped data and a documented constant: replay whole lines of the stored `output` until 32768 is passed and you have N. That is exactly the class the doctrine (F15/lib.rs:136-141) says to recompute rather than persist, and this claim's stated ground for the exemption \u2014 \"unrecoverable from the ledger after the fact\" \u2014 is false there. The conclusion may still be defensible for `look_path` on other grounds (an author-facing label is not a stored derivation to be recomputed by `check`), but the memo does not make that argument, and this claim's argument does not cover half of what the design writes the number into. Grep is untouched by this: the `Search` output is empty and `by_file` is a BTreeMap, so the stdout order the bound consumed is not recoverable from the per-file entries."
15987:     "The conclusion holds; the two-paths distinction the claim draws does not, on the mode axis. C19 says that for `look_grep` the number is \"plainly outside the rule\" because the per-file entries \"are keyed into a `BTreeMap` by filename, so the stdout order the bound consumed is not in the ledger and N is unrecoverable from it\", and reserves the two fallback grounds for `look_path`. `look_grep` is two instruments selected by one argument value: `-r` is pushed only `if root_path.is_dir()` (observe.rs:352-353) and `Exclusions::decide` returns `None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for a non-directory root, so `look --grep <pattern> <one file>` is a first-class mode, exercised at tests/authoring_cli.rs:473 and :485. In that mode `by_file` has exactly one key and its `Vec<String>` holds every matched line's `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order \u2014 the order the bound consumed \u2014 and the shipped `GrepMatch` entry carries that Vec joined by \"\\n\" as its `output` with `{file} (grep: {pattern})` as its label, so the `{file}:` prefix the bound counted is recoverable too. Full stdout is reconstructible byte-for-byte, and the design's own label states the budget it applied, so replaying the release rule reproduces N exactly. What C19 asserts is unrecoverable is recoverable in this mode. The claim's conclusion survives untouched, because the two grounds it states for `look_path` \u2014 that a replay answers what today's build would show rather than what this author was shown, and that a label's audience holds a rendered memo with no captured output in front of them \u2014 apply verbatim to a single-file grep. The narrowing owed is that the ledger-order argument covers only the recursive mode, and that both paths rest on the same two grounds wherever it does not."
15991:     "Read directly in src/observe.rs. Recursive mode: the Search entry's `output` is `String::new()`, and the per-file entries are collected into `by_file: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>` keyed by filename, so grep's stdout order \u2014 the order a bound would consume \u2014 is not in the ledger. Two instruments by one argument value: `args.push(\"-r\")` runs only inside `if root_path.is_dir()`, and `Exclusions::decide` (observe.rs:240-259) returns `Exclusions::None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for any non-directory root, verbatim. In single-file mode `-H` is pushed unconditionally so every line is `{file}:{lineno}:{text}` and `split_once(':')` yields one constant key, hence exactly one by_file entry whose Vec holds every matched line as `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order, shipped as `output: matches.join(\"\\n\")` under `label: format!(\"{file} (grep: {pattern})\")` \u2014 file, order and every matched line all in the ledger, so the full stdout reconstructs from that one entry. For look_path, `PendingEntry { output: shown, .. }` receives the complete selection."

380:   "text": "This design ran into its own subject before it could declare a single modification target, and the shape of that is worth stating rather than working around quietly. TET-28 requires a symbol an implementer is told to modify to be censused by a grep of the whole worktree. Every candidate symbol here was priced first: `look_grep` costs 709,469 bytes, `NON_COVERAGE` 858,096, `censuses` 691,562, `look_path` 688,776, `search_key` 633,291. The interesting number is not any one of them but the floor they share \u2014 roughly 0.63 MB is returned whichever symbol is asked for, because it is not about the symbol at all. Dropping snapshot directories and evidence ledgers alone removes between 95.9% and 99.9% of each. So the census requirement is today priced by tetel's own accumulated output rather than by the code being censused: two thirds of a megabyte comes back from grep, and is stored in the fact, per declared target.",
474:   "text": "The maintainer's scope sentence \u2014 no `look` should return tetel's own content \u2014 should not become the printed guarantee, because after this change it is false. `look_path` refuses a directory, reads exactly the file it was handed, and traverses nothing; it can and should still open a snapshot's `prose.jsonl` for a reader who names it, which is how anyone re-checks a prior memo's record against what it claims. The design leaves it entirely alone. The honest guarantee covers both modes in one sentence: a `look` returns tetel's own output only when the caller named it. That is not a weaker promise dressed up \u2014 it is the same rule `look_grep` is being given, since what the exclusions remove is only ever reached by traversal, and it happens to be a rule `look_path` has always satisfied trivially. A reader with only the printed sentence to go on is then told the thing that actually determines whether they will see a snapshot: whether they asked for one.",
478:     "clause": "it happens to be a rule `look_path` has always satisfied trivially",
1226:   "text": "The other `look` path turns out to have a different answer from the one its shape suggests. `look_path` computes `shown` and uses it twice, but not as one value in one place: `printed` is a string of its own that receives a *copy* of `shown` by borrow, and only afterwards is `shown` moved into the pending entry's `output`. Two independent strings exist between those two points, so a bound applied to `printed` there leaves the captured output, the label, the key, the extent, the pin and the snapshot byte-identical \u2014 the same separation `look_grep` has, in a function that reads at first glance as though it has none. There is therefore no code-shaped reason to leave the plain `look <path>` alone, and no other reason either: a whole-file read that overruns the caller's cap is the same silent cut this design exists to stop. So it is bounded too, on the same terms.",
1246:   "text": "Two functions change, both in `observe.rs`. A whole-worktree census of `look_grep` finds five occurrences in two source files \u2014 the definition, one call site in `dispatch`, three doc comments \u2014 and a census of `look_path` finds four in one file: the definition, one call site in the same `dispatch`, two doc comments. No test, no binary and no other module names either of them. The bound, the marker in the returned text and the label segment are all assembled inside each function, and neither signature changes, so nothing calling them has to be touched \u2014 not `dispatch`, not the CLI, not the MCP handler.",
1509:   "text": "Where an asymmetry does survive is inside `look_path`, and it is about what a shortfall means rather than about whether the bound applies. Under `--lines A:B` the author named a range, and the label already records that range as delivered \u2014 clamped to the file's length, or an explicit \"nothing in range\" \u2014 so the shortfall it reports is one the author asked for. A bound biting on top of that is a second shortfall, chosen by tetel rather than by them, and it is recorded beside the first rather than in place of it. Under a plain `look <path>` there is no author-named range at all: the bound is the only shortfall there is, and naming it is the only thing standing between the author and a cut they would never learn about. The spelling is the grep case's, on both surfaces: the label reads `<path> \u2014 showed N of M lines (32768-byte bound)`, or `<path> lines {a}-{end} \u2014 showed N of M lines (32768-byte bound)` where a range was asked for, with M the line count of what was selected before the bound; the returned text ends with the same segment. 972:    "prop": "\"Transcribed verbatim\" cannot be an honour-system field, and does not need to be: the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output. Both sides of that comparison are Strings the tool controls \u2014 a fact's output is produced only by look/run (file bytes read verbatim by look_path, grep match lines, a process's merged stream), no authoring surface lets anyone supply output by hand, and output is immutable after mint \u2014 so substring containment is a pure byte-level comparison with no normalisation step owned by the check. Typing is the selection mechanism, not the trust: the author types the premise, but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb. This is exactly the README's Direction item for supporting-span selection (\"refused unless it is a verbatim substring of a cited fact \u2014 the author cannot type an extent, and here could not invent support, only select it\"), and TET-29 is the first place it becomes load-bearing rather than roadmap.",

4423:    "prop": "The strictness objections to byte-level containment dissolve on the actual capture path, and every weaker relation reopens the invention channel. A donor comment wrapped across lines with interior prefix noise (`//`, `*`, indentation) IS a contiguous byte substring of a look_path capture, because look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim \u2014 the cost is only that the selected premise carries its comment syntax into the rendered section, which the \"never paraphrase\" constraint endorses rather than tolerates. Stripping that noise would require knowing each language's comment syntax, which is precisely the hard-coded per-language coupling scope.rs's \"language-agnostic by construction\" doctrine excludes. Two capture modes genuinely fight containment \u2014 grep-derived match outputs interleave \"lineno:\" prefixes between lines, and whole-search/no-match records carry empty output \u2014 so the design's guidance is that a donor fact is minted from `look` of the donor file; that is guidance about which observation to select from, not a new rule, since the relation is indifferent to which kind produced the bytes. Weaker relations fail: per-line containment lets an author stitch non-adjacent lines into a sentence the donor never wrote, and whitespace- or case-normalised matching means the memo shows text the capture does not contain \u2014 both are paraphrase with extra steps.",

4511:        "note": "The capture-path clauses check out with one unstated condition. Grep-derived per-file outputs do carry \"lineno:\" prefixes on every line, and both Search and NoMatch records store empty output \u2014 verified in look_grep. But \"look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim\" is unconditionally true only for the plain open: with --lines, look_path collects contents.lines() and re-joins with \"\\n\", which reproduces the file's bytes for LF files but not for CRLF files (and read_to_string refuses non-UTF-8 entirely). A wrapped donor comment is a contiguous substring of a whole-file capture; for a --lines capture that holds only under the LF condition the proposition does not state."
4519:        "note": "Each capture-mode assertion is what observe.rs does: plain look_path stores fs::read_to_string's contents verbatim (no normalisation); --lines stores all[a-1..end].join(\"\\n\"), and Rust's lines() strips \\r on CRLF and the final join drops the trailing newline \u2014 in that mode only, exactly as claimed. So a multi-line prefixed comment is a contiguous substring of the capture in both modes. The two fighting modes are real too: per-file grep entries join \"lineno:\"-prefixed match lines, and the Search/NoMatch whole-search records carry output: String::new(). The stitching argument against per-line containment follows directly from the \"\\n\"-join."

23642:        "note": "True of the bound in isolation; false of the design, and the prose spends the unqualified form. `facts::mint` computes the pin as sha256 over, for every pending entry, `label` + `world_root` + `world_state` + `output` (facts.rs:417-435, its own comment: \"a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker\"), and copies `label` into the fact's extent (facts.rs:400-411). C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a \"showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)\" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes \u2014 the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests \"what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope\". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches \"would not pin identically\".\n\nThe second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries \"are built separately... neither reads the other\" \u2014 today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value (\"a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer\") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone \u2014 which is the design's own defect back again.\n\nWhat survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

25615:        "note": "This claim instructs an implementer what a declared modification target (`NON_COVERAGE`) must say, and what it specifies is census-shaped while the design is not. Its content sentence is \"a fact's extent records the whole search, and nothing anywhere establishes that the author read all of it\", and the prose spends it the same way (\"the list carries the general statement that a census's return to its author is bounded\"), as does C16 (\"the static list says a census reports the tree minus what tetel withheld\"). But C9 and C20 put `look_path` inside the same bound, and F1(4) confirms a plain `look <path>` is a wholly different act \u2014 no search, no root, no exclusions, an extent naming one file and a range. An implementer who writes the line this claim specifies leaves every bounded path read with no standing statement anywhere in `check`'s non-coverage list, which is the one surface the design nominates for the general case. The single-line decision may well still be right, but the line has to be written for both acts \u2014 \"what `look` returns to its author is bounded, and nothing establishes the author read the whole of what the extent records\" \u2014 not for a census. As it stands the claim's own wording, followed literally, produces a line that covers `look_grep` only."
25619:        "note": "report.rs:86-190 carries both entries and the comment between them verbatim: the platform-accident entry (\"symlinked directories and binary files\"), the tetel-output entry, and \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\". No entry in the list concerns what `look` returned to its author. `look_path` applying no exclusion filtering is F2 and is also stated in the tetel-output entry itself; scope.rs naming interpretation/insincere examination as permanently out of reach is F5."

Reading it as naming the second half (\"a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed, and nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it\") requires stretching \"insincere examination\" from not-examined to not-shown, and scope.rs does not spell that out. 26045:        "note": "The numbers and the unit are confirmed independently (F6): reproducing look_grep's own exclusion set and running the grep gives exactly 883 matching lines and 70 distinct first-colon fields, and appending one trailing parenthesised exclusion-note line raises the distinct-field count to 71, which is the stated cause of the earlier figure. `by_file.len()` is indeed the count of distinct first-colon fields and is computed from the full stdout (F2), and `stdout.lines()` is what look_grep splits on. The clause that does not hold as written is the closing analogy, \"which is how `look --lines` already annotates a range only when it was clamped\": look_path writes `{path} lines {a}-{end}` into the label on every ranged read, clamped or not (observe.rs:308-309), so the range annotation is not clamp-conditional. What is conditional is only the empty-selection form `{path} lines {a}-{b} (file has {total} line(s); nothing in range)`. The analogy therefore overstates the existing convention; the proposed \"absence means whole\" behaviour for the shortfall segment is not itself in question."

26274:        "note": "The `look_path` half of this claim \u2014 \"`--lines A:B` is already a first-class parameter of the same verb, so the author reads the rest of the file by asking for it\" \u2014 is broken by a state reachable on tracked files in this worktree.\n\nConstruction. Take `look /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/docs/design/tet46-look-never-returns-tetel-content.md.tetel/facts.jsonl`. F1(7) measures it: 20 lines, of which two exceed 32768 bytes, the longest 905745. F1(4) confirms `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering of any kind, so a named snapshot path is read like any other file \u2014 nothing stops this call. Under the rule the design states (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\", C5/C20), the return stops at whichever over-budget line comes first. The author then asks for the rest with `--lines k:20`. The selection now BEGINS with a 905745-byte line, no whole line fits under 32768, and the bound admits zero lines: the author gets the `==> path <==` header, an empty body, and a label reading \"showed 0 of N lines (32768-byte bound)\". Every range that includes that line behaves identically. There is no `--lines` argument that returns any byte of it, so the claim's remedy does not reach it, and \"needs nothing new either\" is false: this case needs something the design does not have (a floor of one line, a byte-level fallback for an over-budget line, or at minimum an explicit statement that an over-budget line is unreadable through `look`).\n\nWorse than the status quo on exactly the axis the ticket cares about. Today the caller truncates at ~59 KB, so the author reading that file sees its first ~59 KB. Under the design they see zero bytes of that line. The memo's answer to \"what does an author do\" is that the design \"does not give the author back what was withheld; it stops the withholding from being secret\" \u2014 but here the design withholds strictly more than the status quo did, and this claim asserts a remedy that does not exist.\n\nThe same construction reaches `look_grep`: a grep whose matching line is one of these long JSON lines emits a `<file>:<lineno>:<text>` line over the budget, and if it is the first matching line the bounded return is empty while the label still says \"N files matched\". The prose's consolation that \"even a heavily bounded return still tells the author truthfully how many files matched\" is then a file count attached to nothing."

26525:        "note": "The exemption holds for the grep label and does not extend to the `look_path` label the revision brought inside the bound. Every reason this claim gives is grep-shaped: \"the `Search` entry's `output` is empty and the per-file entries record what was captured, not how much of it was returned\". For `look_path` neither is true. F1(4): the `Path` entry's `output` is `shown` \u2014 the complete selected text, in original order, moved in whole \u2014 and F1(6): facts.jsonl, carrying that output, ships into the snapshot. So for the `look_path` label required by C20, N is a pure function of shipped data and a documented constant: replay whole lines of the stored `output` until 32768 is passed and you have N. That is exactly the class the doctrine (F15/lib.rs:136-141) says to recompute rather than persist, and this claim's stated ground for the exemption \u2014 \"unrecoverable from the ledger after the fact\" \u2014 is false there. The conclusion may still be defensible for `look_path` on other grounds (an author-facing label is not a stored derivation to be recomputed by `check`), but the memo does not make that argument, and this claim's argument does not cover half of what the design writes the number into. Grep is untouched by this: the `Search` output is empty and `by_file` is a BTreeMap, so the stdout order the bound consumed is not recoverable from the per-file entries."
26533:        "note": "The conclusion holds; the two-paths distinction the claim draws does not, on the mode axis. C19 says that for `look_grep` the number is \"plainly outside the rule\" because the per-file entries \"are keyed into a `BTreeMap` by filename, so the stdout order the bound consumed is not in the ledger and N is unrecoverable from it\", and reserves the two fallback grounds for `look_path`. `look_grep` is two instruments selected by one argument value: `-r` is pushed only `if root_path.is_dir()` (observe.rs:352-353) and `Exclusions::decide` returns `None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for a non-directory root, so `look --grep <pattern> <one file>` is a first-class mode, exercised at tests/authoring_cli.rs:473 and :485. In that mode `by_file` has exactly one key and its `Vec<String>` holds every matched line's `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order \u2014 the order the bound consumed \u2014 and the shipped `GrepMatch` entry carries that Vec joined by \"\\n\" as its `output` with `{file} (grep: {pattern})` as its label, so the `{file}:` prefix the bound counted is recoverable too. Full stdout is reconstructible byte-for-byte, and the design's own label states the budget it applied, so replaying the release rule reproduces N exactly. What C19 asserts is unrecoverable is recoverable in this mode. The claim's conclusion survives untouched, because the two grounds it states for `look_path` \u2014 that a replay answers what today's build would show rather than what this author was shown, and that a label's audience holds a rendered memo with no captured output in front of them \u2014 apply verbatim to a single-file grep. The narrowing owed is that the ledger-order argument covers only the recursive mode, and that both paths rest on the same two grounds wherever it does not."
26537:        "note": "Read directly in src/observe.rs. Recursive mode: the Search entry's `output` is `String::new()`, and the per-file entries are collected into `by_file: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>` keyed by filename, so grep's stdout order \u2014 the order a bound would consume \u2014 is not in the ledger. Two instruments by one argument value: `args.push(\"-r\")` runs only inside `if root_path.is_dir()`, and `Exclusions::decide` (observe.rs:240-259) returns `Exclusions::None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for any non-directory root, verbatim. In single-file mode `-H` is pushed unconditionally so every line is `{file}:{lineno}:{text}` and `split_once(':')` yields one constant key, hence exactly one by_file entry whose Vec holds every matched line as `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order, shipped as `output: matches.join(\"\\n\")` under `label: format!(\"{file} (grep: {pattern})\")` \u2014 file, order and every matched line all in the ledger, so the full stdout reconstructs from that one entry. For look_path, `PendingEntry { output: shown, .. }` receives the complete selection."

596:    "prop": "The strictness objections to byte-level containment dissolve on the actual capture path, and every weaker relation reopens the invention channel. A donor comment wrapped across lines with interior prefix noise (`//`, `*`, indentation) IS a contiguous byte substring of a look_path capture, because look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim \u2014 the cost is only that the selected premise carries its comment syntax into the rendered section, which the \"never paraphrase\" constraint endorses rather than tolerates. Stripping that noise would require knowing each language's comment syntax, which is precisely the hard-coded per-language coupling scope.rs's \"language-agnostic by construction\" doctrine excludes. Two capture modes genuinely fight containment \u2014 grep-derived match outputs interleave \"lineno:\" prefixes between lines, and whole-search/no-match records carry empty output \u2014 so the design's guidance is that a donor fact is minted from `look` of the donor file; that is guidance about which observation to select from, not a new rule, since the relation is indifferent to which kind produced the bytes. Weaker relations fail: per-line containment lets an author stitch non-adjacent lines into a sentence the donor never wrote, and whitespace- or case-normalised matching means the memo shows text the capture does not contain \u2014 both are paraphrase with extra steps.",
608:        "note": "The capture-path clauses check out with one unstated condition. Grep-derived per-file outputs do carry \"lineno:\" prefixes on every line, and both Search and NoMatch records store empty output \u2014 verified in look_grep. But \"look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim\" is unconditionally true only for the plain open: with --lines, look_path collects contents.lines() and re-joins with \"\\n\", which reproduces the file's bytes for LF files but not for CRLF files (and read_to_string refuses non-UTF-8 entirely). A wrapped donor comment is a contiguous substring of a whole-file capture; for a --lines capture that holds only under the LF condition the proposition does not state."
616:        "note": "Each capture-mode assertion is what observe.rs does: plain look_path stores fs::read_to_string's contents verbatim (no normalisation); --lines stores all[a-1..end].join(\"\\n\"), and Rust's lines() strips \\r on CRLF and the final join drops the trailing newline \u2014 in that mode only, exactly as claimed. So a multi-line prefixed comment is a contiguous substring of the capture in both modes. The two fighting modes are real too: per-file grep entries join \"lineno:\"-prefixed match lines, and the Search/NoMatch whole-search records carry output: String::new(). The stitching argument against per-line containment follows directly from the \"\\n\"-join."
782:        "note": "The \"raw capture\" premise holds: a plain look_path capture stores the donor file's bytes verbatim, so both the single-line clause and the full seven-line comment with its // prefixes are contiguous substrings of such a capture, with no comment-syntax knowledge involved."

3938:        "note": "The `look_path` half of this claim \u2014 \"`--lines A:B` is already a first-class parameter of the same verb, so the author reads the rest of the file by asking for it\" \u2014 is broken by a state reachable on tracked files in this worktree.\n\nConstruction. F1(7) measures it: 20 lines, of which two exceed 32768 bytes, the longest 905745. F1(4) confirms `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering of any kind, so a named snapshot path is read like any other file \u2014 nothing stops this call. Under the rule the design states (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\", C5/C20), the return stops at whichever over-budget line comes first. The author then asks for the rest with `--lines k:20`. The selection now BEGINS with a 905745-byte line, no whole line fits under 32768, and the bound admits zero lines: the author gets the `==> path <==` header, an empty body, and a label reading \"showed 0 of N lines (32768-byte bound)\". Every range that includes that line behaves identically. There is no `--lines` argument that returns any byte of it, so the claim's remedy does not reach it, and \"needs nothing new either\" is false: this case needs something the design does not have (a floor of one line, a byte-level fallback for an over-budget line, or at minimum an explicit statement that an over-budget line is unreadable through `look`).\n\nWorse than the status quo on exactly the axis the ticket cares about. Today the caller truncates at ~59 KB, so the author reading that file sees its first ~59 KB. Under the design they see zero bytes of that line. The memo's answer to \"what does an author do\" is that the design \"does not give the author back what was withheld; it stops the withholding from being secret\" \u2014 but here the design withholds strictly more than the status quo did, and this claim asserts a remedy that does not exist.\n\nThe same construction reaches `look_grep`: a grep whose matching line is one of these long JSON lines emits a `<file>:<lineno>:<text>` line over the budget, and if it is the first matching line the bounded return is empty while the label still says \"N files matched\". The prose's consolation that \"even a heavily bounded return still tells the author truthfully how many files matched\" is then a file count attached to nothing."

620:    "prop": "\"Transcribed verbatim\" cannot be an honour-system field, and does not need to be: the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output. Typing is the selection mechanism, not the trust: the author types the premise, but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb. This is exactly the README's Direction item for supporting-span selection (\"refused unless it is a verbatim substring of a cited fact \u2014 the author cannot type an extent, and here could not invent support, only select it\"), and TET-29 is the first place it becomes load-bearing rather than roadmap.",
660:    "prop": "The strictness objections to byte-level containment dissolve on the actual capture path, and every weaker relation reopens the invention channel. Stripping that noise would require knowing each language's comment syntax, which is precisely the hard-coded per-language coupling scope.rs's \"language-agnostic by construction\" doctrine excludes. Two capture modes genuinely fight containment \u2014 grep-derived match outputs interleave \"lineno:\" prefixes between lines, and whole-search/no-match records carry empty output \u2014 so the design's guidance is that a donor fact is minted from `look` of the donor file; that is guidance about which observation to select from, not a new rule, since the relation is indifferent to which kind produced the bytes. In single-file mode `-H` is pushed unconditionally so every line is `{file}:{lineno}:{text}` and `split_once(':')` yields one constant key, hence exactly one by_file entry whose Vec holds every matched line as `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order, shipped as `output: matches.join(\"\\n\")` under `label: format!(\"{file} (grep: {pattern})\")` \u2014 file, order and every matched line all in the ledger, so the full stdout reconstructs from that one entry. 636:    "prop": "\"Transcribed verbatim\" cannot be an honour-system field, and does not need to be: the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output. Both sides of that comparison are Strings the tool controls \u2014 a fact's output is produced only by look/run (file bytes read verbatim by look_path, grep match lines, a process's merged stream), no authoring surface lets anyone supply output by hand, and output is immutable after mint \u2014 so substring containment is a pure byte-level comparison with no normalisation step owned by the check. Typing is the selection mechanism, not the trust: the author types the premise, but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb. This is exactly the README's Direction item for supporting-span selection (\"refused unless it is a verbatim substring of a cited fact \u2014 the author cannot type an extent, and here could not invent support, only select it\"), and TET-29 is the first place it becomes load-bearing rather than roadmap.",
683:    "prop": "The strictness objections to byte-level containment dissolve on the actual capture path, and every weaker relation reopens the invention channel. A donor comment wrapped across lines with interior prefix noise (`//`, `*`, indentation) IS a contiguous byte substring of a look_path capture, because look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim \u2014 the cost is only that the selected premise carries its comment syntax into the rendered section, which the \"never paraphrase\" constraint endorses rather than tolerates. Stripping that noise would require knowing each language's comment syntax, which is precisely the hard-coded per-language coupling scope.rs's \"language-agnostic by construction\" doctrine excludes. Two capture modes genuinely fight containment \u2014 grep-derived match outputs interleave \"lineno:\" prefixes between lines, and whole-search/no-match records carry empty output \u2014 so the design's guidance is that a donor fact is minted from `look` of the donor file; that is guidance about which observation to select from, not a new rule, since the relation is indifferent to which kind produced the bytes. Weaker relations fail: per-line containment lets an author stitch non-adjacent lines into a sentence the donor never wrote, and whitespace- or case-normalised matching means the memo shows text the capture does not contain \u2014 both are paraphrase with extra steps.",
696:        "note": "The capture-path clauses check out with one unstated condition. Grep-derived per-file outputs do carry \"lineno:\" prefixes on every line, and both Search and NoMatch records store empty output \u2014 verified in look_grep. But \"look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim\" is unconditionally true only for the plain open: with --lines, look_path collects contents.lines() and re-joins with \"\\n\", which reproduces the file's bytes for LF files but not for CRLF files (and read_to_string refuses non-UTF-8 entirely). A wrapped donor comment is a contiguous substring of a whole-file capture; for a --lines capture that holds only under the LF condition the proposition does not state."
704:        "note": "Each capture-mode assertion is what observe.rs does: plain look_path stores fs::read_to_string's contents verbatim (no normalisation); --lines stores all[a-1..end].join(\"\\n\"), and Rust's lines() strips \\r on CRLF and the final join drops the trailing newline \u2014 in that mode only, exactly as claimed. So a multi-line prefixed comment is a contiguous substring of the capture in both modes. The two fighting modes are real too: per-file grep entries join \"lineno:\"-prefixed match lines, and the Search/NoMatch whole-search records carry output: String::new(). The stitching argument against per-line containment follows directly from the \"\\n\"-join."
906:        "note": "The \"raw capture\" premise holds: a plain look_path capture stores the donor file's bytes verbatim, so both the single-line clause and the full seven-line comment with its // prefixes are contiguous substrings of such a capture, with no comment-syntax knowledge involved."

2311:    "prop": "No opt-out flag should be added, because three escape hatches already exist and each is reached by naming something rather than by setting a flag. `look_path` opens any single named file, including one inside a snapshot, and is untouched by this design. `look --grep` rooted at a path that is itself tetel content passes no exclusions at all, which is not merely permitted but forced: grep's `--exclude-dir` suppresses a directory named as the recursion root, so the flags must be withheld there or naming a snapshot directory would return nothing. 4460:        "note": "The `look_path` half of this claim \u2014 \"`--lines A:B` is already a first-class parameter of the same verb, so the author reads the rest of the file by asking for it\" \u2014 is broken by a state reachable on tracked files in this worktree.\n\nConstruction. 608:        "note": "The capture-path clauses check out with one unstated condition. 616:        "note": "Each capture-mode assertion is what observe.rs does: plain look_path stores fs::read_to_string's contents verbatim (no normalisation); --lines stores all[a-1..end].join(\"\\n\"), and Rust's lines() strips \\r on CRLF and the final join drops the trailing newline \u2014 in that mode only, exactly as claimed. 782:        "note": "The \"raw capture\" premise holds: a plain look_path capture stores the donor file's bytes verbatim, so both the single-line clause and the full seven-line comment with its // prefixes are contiguous substrings of such a capture, with no comment-syntax knowledge involved."

3915:        "note": "The numbers and the unit are confirmed independently (F6): reproducing look_grep's own exclusion set and running the grep gives exactly 883 matching lines and 70 distinct first-colon fields, and appending one trailing parenthesised exclusion-note line raises the distinct-field count to 71, which is the stated cause of the earlier figure. `by_file.len()` is indeed the count of distinct first-colon fields and is computed from the full stdout (F2), and `stdout.lines()` is what look_grep splits on. 3938:        "note": "The `look_path` half of this claim \u2014 \"`--lines A:B` is already a first-class parameter of the same verb, so the author reads the rest of the file by asking for it\" \u2014 is broken by a state reachable on tracked files in this worktree.\n\nConstruction. F1(7) measures it: 20 lines, of which two exceed 32768 bytes, the longest 905745. Under the rule the design states (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\", C5/C20), the return stops at whichever over-budget line comes first. The author then asks for the rest with `--lines k:20`. The selection now BEGINS with a 905745-byte line, no whole line fits under 32768, and the bound admits zero lines: the author gets the `==> path <==` header, an empty body, and a label reading \"showed 0 of N lines (32768-byte bound)\". There is no `--lines` argument that returns any byte of it, so the claim's remedy does not reach it, and \"needs nothing new either\" is false: this case needs something the design does not have (a floor of one line, a byte-level fallback for an over-budget line, or at minimum an explicit statement that an over-budget line is unreadable through `look`).\n\nWorse than the status quo on exactly the axis the ticket cares about. Today the caller truncates at ~59 KB, so the author reading that file sees its first ~59 KB. Under the design they see zero bytes of that line. The memo's answer to \"what does an author do\" is that the design \"does not give the author back what was withheld; it stops the withholding from being secret\" \u2014 but here the design withholds strictly more than the status quo did, and this claim asserts a remedy that does not exist.\n\nThe same construction reaches `look_grep`: a grep whose matching line is one of these long JSON lines emits a `<file>:<lineno>:<text>` line over the budget, and if it is the first matching line the bounded return is empty while the label still says \"N files matched\". For `look_path` neither is true. F1(4): the `Path` entry's `output` is `shown` \u2014 the complete selected text, in original order, moved in whole \u2014 and F1(6): facts.jsonl, carrying that output, ships into the snapshot. So for the `look_path` label required by C20, N is a pure function of shipped data and a documented constant: replay whole lines of the stored `output` until 32768 is passed and you have N. That is exactly the class the doctrine (F15/lib.rs:136-141) says to recompute rather than persist, and this claim's stated ground for the exemption \u2014 \"unrecoverable from the ledger after the fact\" \u2014 is false there. The conclusion may still be defensible for `look_path` on other grounds (an author-facing label is not a stored derivation to be recomputed by `check`), but the memo does not make that argument, and this claim's argument does not cover half of what the design writes the number into. 3981:        "note": "The conclusion holds; the two-paths distinction the claim draws does not, on the mode axis. C19 says that for `look_grep` the number is \"plainly outside the rule\" because the per-file entries \"are keyed into a `BTreeMap` by filename, so the stdout order the bound consumed is not in the ledger and N is unrecoverable from it\", and reserves the two fallback grounds for `look_path`. `look_grep` is two instruments selected by one argument value: `-r` is pushed only `if root_path.is_dir()` (observe.rs:352-353) and `Exclusions::decide` returns `None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for a non-directory root, so `look --grep <pattern> <one file>` is a first-class mode, exercised at tests/authoring_cli.rs:473 and :485. In that mode `by_file` has exactly one key and its `Vec<String>` holds every matched line's `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order \u2014 the order the bound consumed \u2014 and the shipped `GrepMatch` entry carries that Vec joined by \"\\n\" as its `output` with `{file} (grep: {pattern})` as its label, so the `{file}:` prefix the bound counted is recoverable too. Full stdout is reconstructible byte-for-byte, and the design's own label states the budget it applied, so replaying the release rule reproduces N exactly. What C19 asserts is unrecoverable is recoverable in this mode. The claim's conclusion survives untouched, because the two grounds it states for `look_path` \u2014 that a replay answers what today's build would show rather than what this author was shown, and that a label's audience holds a rendered memo with no captured output in front of them \u2014 apply verbatim to a single-file grep. The narrowing owed is that the ledger-order argument covers only the recursive mode, and that both paths rest on the same two grounds wherever it does not."
3985:        "note": "Read directly in src/observe.rs. Recursive mode: the Search entry's `output` is `String::new()`, and the per-file entries are collected into `by_file: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>` keyed by filename, so grep's stdout order \u2014 the order a bound would consume \u2014 is not in the ledger. Two instruments by one argument value: `args.push(\"-r\")` runs only inside `if root_path.is_dir()`, and `Exclusions::decide` (observe.rs:240-259) returns `Exclusions::None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for any non-directory root, verbatim. For look_path, `PendingEntry { output: shown, .. }` receives the complete selection."

"Transcribed verbatim" cannot be an honour-system field, and does not need to be: the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output. Both sides of that comparison are Strings the tool controls — a fact's output is produced only by look/run (file bytes read verbatim by look_path, grep match lines, a process's merged stream), no authoring surface lets anyone supply output by hand, and output is immutable after mint — so substring containment is a pure byte-level comparison with no normalisation step owned by the check. Typing is the selection mechanism, not the trust: the author types the premise, but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb. This is exactly the README's Direction item for supporting-span selection ("refused unless it is a verbatim substring of a cited fact — the author cannot type an extent, and here could not invent support, only select it"), and TET-29 is the first place it becomes load-bearing rather than roadmap.

How grep spells the names it matches --exclude against, measured on /usr/bin/grep (BSD 2.6.0-FreeBSD) in the same scratch tree, extended with other/memo.md — a file that contains "NEEDLE here" and has NO sibling other/memo.md.tetel directory (`ls -d other/memo.md.tetel` reports No such file or directory), so it is not a rendered memo under the ticket's own iff test.

(A) With the search root given as the relative "." and --exclude given as the ABSOLUTE path of docs/design/memo.md, nothing was excluded — all 7 files matched, including docs/design/memo.md. The exclusion silently did nothing.
(B) With the same relative root "." and --exclude given as './docs/design/memo.md' — the same spelling grep constructs for the file when walking from "." — docs/design/memo.md was excluded and everything else remained.
(C) With an absolute root and --exclude='memo.md', a bare basename, BOTH docs/design/memo.md and other/memo.md were excluded.

So the pattern must be spelled the way grep will construct the file's name from the root as given, and a bare basename over-excludes files that are not rendered memos.

Two existing mechanisms that an exclusion disclosure could ride on without a schema change.

(1) compose.rs `render_facts` (lines 205-275 of src/compose.rs): the rendered memo's "## Facts" table has a column "Extent (captured)" whose cell is built by mapping each extent entry to `e.label` and joining with "; ". Its doc comment states explicitly that only the label is rendered, never the `key` (an absolute machine-local path) and never the captured output. So whatever a `look` writes into an extent entry's `label` reaches every reader of the committed memo; whatever it writes anywhere else does not.

(2) facts.rs `mint` (lines 413-437 of src/facts.rs): the pin is sha256 over a string built per pending entry from, in order, `label`, `world_root`, `world_state`, `output`, each newline-terminated. The label is therefore already inside the pin. So a label that names the exclusion set makes two searches with different exclusion sets pin differently even when their matched output is identical.

25:The predicate has one soundness worry worth retiring now: it compares a filesystem-canonicalized path against git's own spelling of the toplevel, and those are produced by two different tools. A live probe against this repository shows them agreeing byte-for-byte, and the failure mode if they ever disagree is the right one — inequality can only deny rooting, so a spelling divergence refuses an honest census loudly instead of accepting an unrooted one silently. Two hardenings close the gap: look_grep itself compares the canonicalized search root against the marker's root at capture time and stores the search entry's key in the marker's spelling when both name the same directory, leaving check a pure byte comparison; and the agreement is pinned by a test rather than assumed, since one probe on one machine establishes the common case, not an invariant.
84:| C2 | TET-28's "workspace-rooted" requirement is NOT decidable from today's capture in the case that matters most. When look_grep finds matches, it records one extent entry per matched file, keyed on that file's resolved path, with label "<file> (grep: <pattern>)" — and the search root appears nowhere in what is captured; the code's own comment says the entries are keyed "not by the search root or the grep command line". A repo-wide grep and a single-file grep that matched the same file therefore capture byte-identical extents. Every genuine census of a symbol an implementer is told to modify falls in this positive-match case, because the symbol's definition site matches. | OWED |
86:| C4 | The census therefore needs a small capture extension before any refusal can exist: look_grep should record, for every search, one root-level search entry — key = the resolved search root, a label carrying the pattern and the match-file count, marker resolved from the search root — alongside the existing per-file match entries, making the match and no-match cases uniform. "Workspace-rooted" then has one decidable definition covering both cases: the search entry's key equals its own world_root, a byte comparison of two strings the same look_grep call captured from the same canonicalized directory. No author-typed input participates on either side. | OWED |

Two hardenings belong in the implementation: look_grep should itself compare the canonicalized search root against the marker's root at capture time and store the search entry's key in the marker's spelling when they name the same directory, so check stays a pure byte comparison; and the agreement should be pinned by a test, since one probe on one machine shows the common case, not an invariant. | OWED |

97:| C15 | A census enumerates call sites, not the modes those sites select, and this is a distinct printed limit rather than the insincere-examination ceiling restated. Distinct because the two limits bound different things: the ceiling bounds interpretation — capture makes the extent honest, not the reading of it — while the mode limit bounds the artifact itself. What look_grep captures per matched file is the matching lines only; an argument that selects materially different behaviour (a None versus a Some, a flag, a mode enum) is sometimes visible on a match line, never enumerated, and absent entirely when the value arrives through a variable, a default, or another line of a multi-line call. So even a sincerely read census does not, in general, contain which mechanism each caller engages — the reader must leave the census and read the callee and each call's context, which is why collapsing this into "whether anyone read the census" would misstate the remedy. First, the trigger: \"any design that transplants\" is as undecidable from prose as \"a memo's recommendation\" was for TET-28, so the trigger is an author-declared transplant record, and the refusal attaches to declarations. Second, and largest: \"transcribed verbatim\" cannot be a typed field on trust — a premise is refused unless its text is a verbatim substring of one observation's captured output inside the cited donor fact, which converts transcription from a request into a machine guarantee and makes TET-29 the first load-bearing use of the README's supporting-span-selection direction. This recovers the same signal at grading time, when nobody is\\n/// relying on the author's attention: `FactEvent::Create` carries a\\n/// timestamp that ships in `facts.jsonl`, and the snapshot copies\\n/// `refusals.log` beside it, so the windows are derivable from files\\n/// every snapshot already contains. No schema change, nothing new stored.\\n///\\n/// Human-owed and verbatim: a mint following a refusal is frequently\\n/// correct, and which of them matters is a reader's call. Nothing here\\n/// counts, scores or ranks.\\n///\\n/// The listing is only ever as complete as the log beneath it — a\\n/// snapshot written by a build that did not record surface-layer\\n/// refusals simply has fewer lines, and this is silent about them. That\\n/// is not a completeness claim in either direction: a verbatim listing\\n/// asserts only what was recorded.\\npub fn mint_windows(snapshot_dir: &Path) -> Vec<MintWindow> {\\n    let Ok(events) = workspace::read_jsonl::<FactEvent>(&log_path(snapshot_dir)) else {\\n        return Vec::new();\\n    };\\n    let mints: Vec<(String, u64)> = events\\n        .iter()\\n        .filter_map(|e| match e {\\n            FactEvent::Create { id, timestamp, .. } => Some((id.clone(), *timestamp)),\\n            FactEvent::Revise { .. } => None,\\n        })\\n        .collect();\\n\\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\\n    for (i, (id, minted_at)) in mints.iter().enumerate() {\\n        // The window opens at the previous mint — or at the beginning of\\n        // the log for the first fact, which owns everything refused\\n        // before it.\\n        let opened = if i == 0 { None } else { Some(mints[i - 1].1) };\\n        let stamped: Vec<(u64, String)> = workspace::refusals_since(snapshot_dir, opened)\\n            .into_iter()\\n            .filter_map(|line| {\\n                let ts = line.split_once('\\\\t').and_then(|(ts, _)| ts.parse::<u64>().ok())?;\\n                (ts <= *minted_at).then_some((ts, line))\\n            })\\n            .collect();\\n        if !stamped.is_empty() {\\n            let straddles_a_boundary = stamped\\n                .iter()\\n                .any(|(ts, _)| *ts == *minted_at || opened.is_some_and(|o| *ts == o));\\n            out.push(MintWindow {\\n                fact_id: id.clone(),\\n                refusals: stamped.into_iter().map(|(_, line)| line).collect(),\\n                is_first: i == 0,\\n                straddles_a_boundary,\\n            });\\n        }\\n    }\\n    out\\n}\\n\\n/// Mint a fact from the current pending buffer. Refuses if the buffer\\n/// is empty (a fact needs a preceding `look`/`run`) or the note text is\\n/// empty. Clears the buffer on success, exactly once, after the log\\n/// append succeeds — never before.\\npub fn mint(workspace_dir: &Path, note: &str) -> Result<Fact, AuthoringError> {\\n    if note.trim().is_empty() {\\n        return Err(workspace::refuse(workspace_dir, \\\"fact\\\", \\\"note text is empty\\\"));\\n    }\\n    let buf = pending::load(workspace_dir)?;\\n    if buf.is_empty() {\\n        return Err(workspace::refuse(\\n            workspace_dir,\\n            \\\"fact\\\",\\n            \\\"pending observation buffer is empty; run `tetel look` or `tetel run` first, then `tetel fact`\\\",\\n        ));\\n    }\\n\\n    let extent: Vec<ExtentEntry> = buf\\n        .iter()\\n        .map(|e| ExtentEntry {\\n            key: e.key.clone(),\\n            label: e.label.clone(),\\n            world_root: e.world_root.clone(),\\n            world_state: e.world_state.clone(),\\n            kind: Some(e.kind),\\n            pattern: e.pattern.clone(),\\n        })\\n        .collect();\\n    let output = buf.iter().filter(|e| !e.output.is_empty()).map(|e| e.output.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\\\"\\\\n\\\");\\n\\n    // The pin: a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output\\n    // and world-tree marker — the prototype's compute_pin hashed\\n    // extent labels and captured output; folding the marker in too means\\n    // a fact minted against a different tree state pins differently even\\n    // if its labels/output happen to coincide. Both halves of the marker\\n    // go in: two observations of the same path under the same state but\\n    // in two different checkouts are two different observations. The\\n    // marker itself is still carried separately in `extent` (see\\n    // `ExtentEntry`), since a hash alone can't be compared by a human\\n    // without recomputing it — fix 1 is about visibility, not just\\n    // detectability.\\n    let mut hash_input = String::new();\\n    for e in &buf {\\n        hash_input.push_str(&e.label);\\n        hash_input.push('\\\\n');\\n        hash_input.push_str(&e.world_root);\\n        hash_input.push('\\\\n');\\n        hash_input.push_str(&e.world_state);\\n        hash_input.push('\\\\n');\\n        hash_input.push_str(&e.output);\\n        hash_input.push('\\\\n');\\n    }\\n    let pin = format!(\\\"sha256:{}\\\", sha256_hex(&hash_input));\\n\\n    let id = workspace::next_id(workspace_dir, Kind::Fact)?;\\n    let event = FactEvent::Create {\\n        id: id.clone(),\\n        note: note.to_string(),\\n        extent: extent.clone(),\\n        output: output.clone(),\\n        pin: pin.clone(),\\n        timestamp: workspace::now_unix(),\\n    };\\n    workspace::append_jsonl(&log_path(workspace_dir), &event)?;\\n    pending::clear(workspace_dir)?;\\n\\n    Ok(Fact { id, note: note.to_string(), extent, output, pin, revisions: 0 })\\n}\\n\\n/// `tetel fact --revise <id> --note <new-text> --why <text>`.\\npub fn revise(workspace_dir: &Path, id: &str, new_note: &str, why: &str) -> Result<(), AuthoringError> {\\n    if !exists(workspace_dir, id)? {\\n        return Err(workspace::refuse(workspace_dir, \\\"fact\\\", format!(\\\"no such fact: {id}\\\")));\\n    }\\n    if why.trim().is_empty() {\\n        return Err(workspace::refuse(workspace_dir, \\\"fact\\\", \\\"--revise requires --why (revisions must explain themselves)\\\"));\\n    }\\n    if new_note.trim().is_empty() {\\n        return Err(workspace::refuse(workspace_dir, \\\"fact\\\", \\\"no new --note text given\\\"));\\n    }\\n    let event =\\n        FactEvent::Revise { id: id.to_string(), note: new_note.to_string(), why: why.to_string(), timestamp: workspace::now_unix() };\\n    workspace::append_jsonl(&log_path(workspace_dir), &event)?;\\n    Ok(())\\n}\\n\\n/// What `tetel fact` was asked to do — mint a new fact from the pending\\n/// buffer, or revise an existing one's note. The single shape both the\\n/// CLI and the MCP server build and pass to [`dispatch`], so the two\\n/// front ends can never drift on which combination of missing flags gets\\n/// refused, or with what text.\\npub enum FactRequest {\\n    Mint { note: Option<String> },\\n    Revise { id: String, note: Option<String>, why: Option<String> },\\n}\\n\\npub enum FactOutcome {\\n    Minted(Fact),\\n    Revised { id: String },\\n}\\n\\n/// Dispatches a [`FactRequest`] to [`mint`] or [`revise`], refusing with\\n/// the exact text the CLI has always printed for a flag a mode required\\n/// but didn't get — lifted here (rather than left as a bare `eprintln!`\\n/// in `main.rs`) so the MCP server's structured refusals carry the same\\n/// guidance the CLI does, from the one place that decides it.\\npub fn dispatch(workspace_dir: &Path, req: FactRequest) -> Result<FactOutcome, AuthoringError> {\\n    match req {\\n        FactRequest::Mint { note } => {\\n            let note = note.ok_or_else(|| workspace::refuse(workspace_dir, \\\"fact\\\", \\\"fact requires --note\\\"))?;\\n            mint(workspace_dir, &note).map(FactOutcome::Minted)\\n        }\\n        FactRequest::Revise { id, note, why } => {\\n            let why = why.ok_or_else(|| workspace::refuse(workspace_dir, \\\"fact\\\", \\\"fact --revise requires --why\\\"))?;\\n            let note = note.ok_or_else(|| {\\n                workspace::refuse(workspace_dir, \\\"fact\\\", \\\"fact --revise requires --note (the new note text)\\\")\\n            })?;\\n            revise(workspace_dir, &id, &note, &why).map(|()| FactOutcome::Revised { id })\\n        }\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n#[cfg(test)]\\nmod window_tests {\\n    use super::*;\\n\\n    fn scratch(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {\\n        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\\n            \\\"tetel-window-{tag}-{}-{}\\\",\\n            std::process::id(),\\n            std::time::SystemTime::now()\\n                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\\n                .unwrap()\\n                .as_nanos()\\n        ));\\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();\\n        dir\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Facts as raw `Create` events at chosen timestamps, plus a refusal\\n    /// log at chosen timestamps — the two files a snapshot ships. Written\\n    /// by hand because the whole point is controlling the seconds, which\\n    /// an end-to-end run cannot do.\\n    fn seed(dir: &Path, mints: &[(&str, u64)], refusals: &[(u64, &str)]) {\\n        let facts: String = mints\\n            .iter()\\n            .map(|(id, ts)| {\\n                format!(\\n                    r#\\\"{{\\\"event\\\":\\\"Create\\\",\\\"id\\\":\\\"{id}\\\",\\\"note\\\":\\\"n\\\",\\\"extent\\\":[],\\\"output\\\":\\\"\\\",\\\"pin\\\":\\\"p\\\",\\\"timestamp\\\":{ts}}}\\\"#\\n                ) + \\\"\\\\n\\\"\\n            })\\n            .collect();\\n        std::fs::write(dir.join(\\\"facts.jsonl\\\"), facts).unwrap();\\n        let log: String =\\n            refusals.iter().map(|(ts, r)| format!(\\\"{ts}\\\\tlook\\\\t{r}\\\\n\\\")).collect();\\n        std::fs::write(dir.join(\\\"refusals.log\\\"), log).unwrap();\\n    }\\n\\n    #[test]\\n    fn each_refusal_lands_in_the_window_of_the_mint_that_followed_it() {\\n        let dir = scratch(\\\"attribution\\\");\\n        seed(&dir, &[(\\\"F1\\\", 100), (\\\"F2\\\", 200)], &[(50, \\\"before F1\\\"), (150, \\\"between F1 and F2\\\")]);\\n\\n        let w = mint_windows(&dir);\\n        assert_eq!(w.len(), 2, \\\"both facts have a refusal in their window\\\");\\n        assert_eq!(w[0].fact_id, \\\"F1\\\");\\n        assert!(w[0].is_first, \\\"F1 has no previous mint to open at\\\");\\n        assert!(w[0].refusals[0].contains(\\\"before F1\\\"));\\n        assert_eq!(w[0].refusals.len(), 1, \\\"F1 must not claim a refusal that followed it\\\");\\n        assert_eq!(w[1].fact_id, \\\"F2\\\");\\n        assert!(!w[1].is_first);\\n        assert!(w[1].refusals[0].contains(\\\"between F1 and F2\\\"));\\n        assert_eq!(w[1].refusals.len(), 1);\\n        assert!(!w[0].straddles_a_boundary && !w[1].straddles_a_boundary, \\\"no shared seconds here\\\");\\n\\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\\n    }\\n\\n    /// A refusal sharing a second with a mint cannot be placed on one\\n    /// side of it. It is listed under both adjacent facts and the report\\n    /// says why, rather than a guess being made silently — the same\\n    /// choice the mint-time replay makes.\\n    #[test]\\n    fn a_refusal_sharing_a_second_with_a_mint_is_flagged_not_guessed() {\\n        let dir = scratch(\\\"straddle\\\");\\n        seed(&dir, &[(\\\"F1\\\", 100), (\\\"F2\\\", 200)], &[(100, \\\"same second as F1\\\")]);\\n\\n        let w = mint_windows(&dir);\\n        assert_eq!(w.len(), 2, \\\"listed under both, since which side it fell on is unknowable\\\");\\n        assert!(w[0].straddles_a_boundary, \\\"F1's window closes at this second\\\");\\n        assert!(w[1].straddles_a_boundary, \\\"F2's window opens at it\\\");\\n\\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\\n    }\\n\\n    /// A fact with nothing refused in its window is not listed at all. An\\n    /// entry per fact saying \\\"none\\\" is noise, and noise is what makes a\\n    /// real one invisible.\\n    #[test]\\n    fn a_fact_with_a_clean_window_is_absent_rather_than_reported_empty() {\\n        let dir = scratch(\\\"clean\\\");\\n        seed(&dir, &[(\\\"F1\\\", 100), (\\\"F2\\\", 200)], &[(150, \\\"only in F2's window\\\")]);\\n        let w = mint_windows(&dir);\\n        assert_eq!(w.len(), 1);\\n        assert_eq!(w[0].fact_id, \\\"F2\\\");\\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\\n    }\\n\\n    /// A snapshot from a build that never recorded surface-layer\\n    /// refusals has no log; the listing is silent rather than absent-\\n    /// meaning-clean. A verbatim listing asserts only what was recorded.\\n    #[test]\\n    fn a_snapshot_with_no_refusal_log_yields_no_windows() {\\n        let dir = scratch(\\\"nolog\\\");\\n        seed(&dir, &[(\\\"F1\\\", 100)], &[]);\\n        std::fs::remove_file(dir.join(\\\"refusals.log\\\")).unwrap();\\n        assert!(mint_windows(&dir).is_empty());\\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n//! `tetel look` and `tetel run` — the only two ways an authoring workspace\\n//! adds to its pending observation buffer (see `pending.rs`). Mirrors\\n//! the prototype's `tlook`/`trun`, with two changes: `--lines A:B` is\\n//! new (see the module's `look_path` doc comment), and every recorded\\n//! observation carries a working-tree marker alongside its content\\n//! (fix 1 in the design memo — see `worldstate.rs`).\\n//!\\n//! Each observation resolves its **own** marker, from what it touched: a\\n//! `look` from the file it opened, a `--grep` match from the file it\\n//! matched in, a bounded negative from the search root, and a `run` from\\n//! this process's working directory, which is where the command actually\\n//! ran. Resolving one marker per call and attaching it to everything was\\n//! the original shape and it described the wrong tree — see the measured\\n//! table in `worldstate.rs`.\\n\\nuse std::fs;\\nuse std::io::Read;\\nuse std::path::Path;\\nuse std::process::{Command, Stdio};\\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\\nuse std::thread;\\n\\nuse crate::pending::{self, ObservationKind, PendingEntry};\\nuse crate::workspace::{self, AuthoringError};\\nuse crate::worldstate;\\n\\n/// Resolve `path` to the key used for overlap matching: its canonical\\n/// absolute form when that succeeds, the path as given otherwise.\\n/// Canonicalization can fail on some platforms/filesystems even for a\\n/// path that exists (e.g. a permissions issue on an ancestor\\n/// directory); falling back keeps this infallible rather than losing\\n/// the observation over it.\\nfn resolve_key(path: &Path) -> String {\\n    fs::canonicalize(path).map(|p| p.display().to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|_| path.display().to_string())\\n}\\n\\n/// The key for a whole-search record: the resolved search root, spelled\\n/// the way its own world marker spells the tree root **when the two name\\n/// the same directory**.\\n///\\n/// TET-28's census predicate asks whether a search was rooted at the\\n/// worktree, and answers it by comparing this key against the entry's own\\n/// `world_root`. Both are captured, but by two different tools —\\n/// `fs::canonicalize` here, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` there — and\\n/// nothing guarantees two tools spell one directory identically. Rather\\n/// than have the predicate reason about that, the divergence is resolved\\n/// once, here, where both spellings are in hand.\\n///\\n/// The comparison is on canonicalized forms, so it is about *which\\n/// directory*, never about how either tool wrote it down. When they name\\n/// different directories — a search rooted at a subdirectory, which is\\n/// exactly the case the census exists to catch — the resolved root is\\n/// kept verbatim and the predicate's byte comparison fails, correctly.\\nfn search_key(root: &Path, world_root: &str) -> String {\\n    let resolved = resolve_key(root);\\n    if world_root.is_empty() {\\n        return resolved;\\n    }\\n    let same = fs::canonicalize(root)\\n        .ok()\\n        .zip(fs::canonicalize(world_root).ok())\\n        .map(|(a, b)| a == b)\\n        .unwrap_or(false);\\n    if same { world_root.to_string() } else { resolved }\\n}\\n\\npub struct LookOutcome {\\n    pub printed: String,\\n}\\n\\n/// `tetel look <path> [--lines A:B]`.\\n///\\n/// `--lines A:B` (1-based, inclusive) is new in this port — the\\n/// prototype had no way to bound a read to a range, which forced\\n/// `tetel run sed -n '<range>p' <path>` as a workaround. That workaround\\n/// is exactly what produced fix 2's overlap blind spot (a `proc:`\\n/// observation keyed on the whole `sed` command line never overlapped\\n/// another range of the same file); giving `look` a first-class\\n/// `--lines` removes the reason to reach for `run` here at all, and its\\n/// key is the resolved path regardless of the range requested, so two\\n/// different ranges of one file always overlap each other.\\n///\\n/// A range entirely past the end of the file is not an error — it is\\n/// recorded as an explicit empty-range observation, the same \\\"a bounded\\n/// negative must leave a trace\\\" discipline as a zero-match grep.\\npub fn look_path(workspace_dir: &Path, path: &str, lines: Option<(usize, usize)>) -> Result<LookOutcome, AuthoringError> {\\n    let p = Path::new(path);\\n    if !p.exists() {\\n        return Err(workspace::refuse(workspace_dir, \\\"look\\\", format!(\\\"no such path: {path}\\\")));\\n    }\\n    if p.is_dir() {\\n        return Err(workspace::refuse(\\n            workspace_dir,\\n            \\\"look\\\",\\n            format!(\\n                \\\"{path} is a directory; `tetel look` opens files. Use `tetel look --grep <pattern> {path}` to search it.\\\"\\n            ),\\n        ));\\n    }\\n    let contents = fs::read_to_string(p).map_err(|e| AuthoringError::Io(e.to_string()))?;\\n    let key = resolve_key(p);\\n    // Resolved from the file being read, never from this process's working\\n    // directory — see `worldstate.rs` for the measurement that forced this.\\n    let world = worldstate::Session::new().for_path(p);\\n\\n    let (shown, label) = match lines {\\n        None => (contents.clone(), path.to_string()),\\n        Some((a, b)) => {\\n            if a < 1 || a > b {\\n                return Err(workspace::refuse(workspace_dir, \\\"look\\\", format!(\\\"invalid --lines range {a}:{b}\\\")));\\n            }\\n            let all: Vec<&str> = contents.lines().collect();\\n            let total = all.len();\\n            if a > total {\\n                (String::new(), format!(\\\"{path} lines {a}-{b} (file has {total} line(s); nothing in range)\\\"))\\n            } else {\\n                let end = b.min(total);\\n                (all[a - 1..end].join(\\\"\\\\n\\\"), format!(\\\"{path} lines {a}-{end}\\\"))\\n            }\\n        }\\n    };\\n\\n    let mut printed = String::new();\\n    printed.push_str(&format!(\\\"==> {path} <==\\\\n\\\"));\\n    printed.push_str(&shown);\\n    if !shown.is_empty() && !shown.ends_with('\\\\n') {\\n        printed.push('\\\\n');\\n    }\\n\\n    let entry = PendingEntry {\\n        kind: ObservationKind::Path,\\n        key,\\n        label,\\n        output: shown,\\n        world_root: world.root,\\n        world_state: world.state,\\n        captured_at: workspace::now_unix(),\\n        pattern: String::new(),\\n    };\\n    let mut buf = pending::load(workspace_dir)?;\\n    buf.push(entry);\\n    pending::save(workspace_dir, &buf)?;\\n\\n    Ok(LookOutcome { printed })\\n}\\n\\n/// `tetel look --grep <pattern> <path-or-dir>`.\\n///\\n/// Shells out to the system `grep` (present on every platform this\\n/// crate targets), the same way `run_command` shells out to whatever\\n/// command it's given — reimplementing pattern matching wasn't worth\\n/// the risk of a subtly different regex dialect. A zero-match search\\n/// records an explicit no-match observation (a bounded negative that\\n/// leaves no trace was the specific defect a prior run surfaced); a\\n/// match records one entry per file that actually matched, keyed by\\n/// that file's resolved path (fix 2), not by the search root or the\\n/// grep command line.\\npub fn look_grep(workspace_dir: &Path, pattern: &str, root: &str) -> Result<LookOutcome, AuthoringError> {\\n    let root_path = Path::new(root);\\n    if !root_path.exists() {\\n        return Err(workspace::refuse(workspace_dir, \\\"look\\\", format!(\\\"no such path: {root}\\\")));\\n    }\\n    // One session for the whole search: a recursive grep can match in\\n    // dozens of files, and each matched file resolves its own marker\\n    // (a search root can span a submodule or a nested worktree), but\\n    // files sharing a directory resolve once between them.\\n    let mut world = worldstate::Session::new();\\n\\n    let mut args: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();\\n    if root_path.is_dir() {\\n        args.push(\\\"-r\\\");\\n    }\\n    args.push(\\\"-I\\\");\\n    args.push(\\\"-n\\\");\\n    // `-H` unconditionally, because grep only prints the filename when it\\n    // was given more than one file to search. Without it a search of a\\n    // *single* file returns `<line>:<match>`, and the `split_once(':')`\\n    // below then read the line number as the filename: every such\\n    // observation was keyed on a bare integer, overlapped nothing, and —\\n    // since a bare integer has no parent directory — resolved its\\n    // world-tree marker from this process's working directory, which is\\n    // precisely the defect TET-5 removed everywhere else. The verb refuses everything that is per-record and decidable at creation: a donor fact that does not exist or predates span boundaries, a premise that is not a genuine quotation, a destination that is not a live target, a discharge naming no live claim. text:
Whole-worktree census of the symbol `look_grep`, rooted at /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel — the TET-28 census behind this design's one declared modification target.

What happened when it was taken is itself the observation. `look --grep look_grep /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel` succeeded server-side and recorded the search and its per-file hits into the pending buffer, but the agent harness refused to hand the result back, reporting "result (707,751 characters across 38 lines) exceeds maximum allowed tokens" and spilling it to a file instead. So the author of this memo never read the output of their own census; the 38 matched lines were captured, minted and are shipping in this fact's extent and in the snapshot regardless.

That is the return path and the retention path coming apart under measurement. tetel caps neither: observe.rs pushes the whole stdout into `printed` and the whole per-file output into the pending entries. The only cap in the chain was imposed downstream by the harness, on the return path only, and it fired.

The two code sites the exclusion mechanism has to fit between.

(1) src/facts.rs lines 82-103, `ExtentEntry::censuses` — TET-28's census predicate in full. It reads exactly five things: that `kind` is Some(Search) or Some(NoMatch), that `pattern` byte-equals the symbol, that `world_root` is non-empty and not `worldstate::NO_GIT`, and that `key == world_root`. It never reads `label` and never reads `output`. Its doc comment states the predicate "is about existence and rooting, never about what was found".

(2) src/observe.rs lines 158-195, the head of `look_grep`. It refuses a non-existent root, then builds the argument vector: `-r` ONLY when `root_path.is_dir()`, then `-I`, `-n`, `-H`, `-e`, the pattern, and finally `root` — passed through verbatim as the caller spelled it, never canonicalized. `Command::new("grep")` is then invoked with that vector and the whole stdout is taken with `String::from_utf8_lossy`.

src/observe.rs lines 196-258, the tail of `look_grep` — the return path and the retention path, side by side, with no cap on either.

Return path: on a matching search, `printed.push_str(&stdout)` copies the grep's entire stdout into `printed`, and `printed` is what `LookOutcome` carries back to the caller at the end of the function. There is no length check, no truncation, no elision, and no configuration anywhere between the grep's stdout and that return.

Retention path: separately, the same stdout is split by file and each file's matching lines are pushed into a `PendingEntry` whose `output` is `matches.join("\n")` — also uncapped. The whole-search `Search` entry carries `output: String::new()` and a `label` of the form "search: {root} (grep: {pattern}) — {files} file(s) matched"; the zero-match `NoMatch` entry likewise carries empty output and a "no-match: {pattern} in {root}" label. So the whole-search record is the one entry in a grep's fold that has a label and no output of its own.

Nothing in this function bounds what it returns, and nothing in it records that anything downstream did.
